title: Apple confirms Siri AI launches in English this month, will add five languages in October
snippet: During today’s “Surprise and Shine” event, Apple confirmed the rollout timeline for the new Siri AI, which will launch in English before expanding to five more languages in October. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
During today’s “Surprise and Shine” event, Apple confirmed the rollout timeline for the new Siri AI, which will launch in English before expanding to five more languages in October. Here are the details.

Siri AI language expansion confirmed for October

Apple today announced the iPhone Duo, its first foldable phone, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The company also announced the Apple Watch Series 12 Ultra 4, and AirPods 5 with Active Noise Cancellation.

One thing these devices have in common is the fact that they will rely on one or more capabilities of the new Siri AI, which leverages Apple’s partnership with Google to offer a more capable LLM-based assistant.

Following the original announcement of Siri AI during this year’s WWDC, Apple today confirmed a more precise rollout plan for the languages it will support.

As Apple’s VP of AI Product Marketing Lilian Rincon explained during the event, the new Siri AI will roll out in English alongside the official release of iOS 27, scheduled for September 14, while the following languages will get support for it in October:

French

Japanese

Korean

Portuguese

Spanish

Rincon also confirmed two bits of information Apple’s Craig Federighi first shared during this year’s WWDC.

First, that some features will have usage limits because they rely on powerful server models, and that increased access will be available with most iCloud+ plans.

Second, that Apple Intelligence (of which Siri AI is just a part of) will support the following 16 languages with this month’s OS releases:

English

Chinese (Simplified)

Chinese (Traditional)

Danish

Dutch

French

German

Italian

Japanese

Korean

Norwegian

Portuguese

Spanish

Swedish

Turkish

Vietnamese

Apple notes that Apple Intelligence is not available in China, although the company seems to be working behind the scenes to bring the features to the country. The company also notes that Siri AI will not be available in China, nor in the EU, where Apple and regulators remain at odds over the Digital Markets Act.

title: Two Galaxy S27 models will get Samsung’s Privacy Display, not just the Ultra
snippet: New reports coming from industry sources close to Samsung suggest the smartphone maker will equip not just the Galaxy S27 Ultra with its Privacy Display panels, but the Galaxy S27 Pro, as well. more…
fullText:
New reports coming from industry sources close to Samsung suggest the smartphone maker will equip not just the Galaxy S27 Ultra with its Privacy Display panels, but the Galaxy S27 Pro, as well.

According to recent reports from ET News, industry sources claim Samsung plans to include a Privacy Display panel on the Galaxy S27 Pro and the Galaxy S27 Ultra. The panel is known internally as Samsung’s Flex Magic Panel, and the new leaked information ties it to the top two flagships Samsung wants to release in 2027.

The Privacy Display was earlier in the year on the Galaxy S26 Ultra. In lieu of offering an anti-glare Gorilla Glass panel like the year before, Samsung opted for a specialized OLED panel that obscured either isolated portions or the entire screen from certain angles. It’s a native form of privacy screen protectors, built into the phone, and with more granular controls over sensitive notifications and more.

On the Galaxy S26 Ultra, One UI allows users to hide notifications from prying eyes, as well as the entire screen or other parts that might contain sensitive information. It’s suggested that the Galaxy S27 Pro’s display will allow users to do the same. The COE elements in the display can be thought of as a sort of polarization, where parts of the screen are blocked from anything other than a head-on view.

	

Previous leaks suggest Samsung plans on padding out its smartphone range with four entries:

Galaxy S27

Galaxy S27+

Galaxy S27 Pro

Galaxy S27 Ultra

With that, the Galaxy S27 line will be overhauled with a new display and overall design that many like to compare to the recently adopted design language of recent iPhone versions. The Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra variants will have a much more robust camera bar/island, with the Pro being a much more obvious little brother to the Ultra than the S+ ever was. At least, in looks.

Further, it looks like the Galaxy S27 Pro will take on the Ultra’s price point, and the new premium flagship Galaxy S27 Ultra will get its own price hike.

Samsung is expected to announce the four new Galaxy S27 devices early next year.

title: WhatsApp will soon let users chat with up to five third-party AI agents
snippet: WhatsApp is working on a new feature that will let users connect third-party AI agents to the app, chat with them, and give them instructions to carry out tasks on their behalf. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
WhatsApp is working on a new feature that will let users connect third-party AI agents to the app, chat with them, and give them instructions to carry out tasks on their behalf. Here are the details.

WhatsApp working on third-party agent support

When OpenClaw and similar platforms first exploded in popularity, one of the main ways users interacted with their agents remotely was by connecting them to messaging apps.

However, many users soon discovered that setting up a bot on WhatsApp to talk to third-party AI agents could get the WhatsApp account banned.

Telegram, meanwhile, embraced the trend and has since become one of the main platforms users rely on to chat with, or give instructions to, agents running either locally on their computers or in the cloud.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is working on bringing native support for third-party AI agents to its users, with a new feature that lets them connect agents directly to dedicated chats in the app.

Image: WABetaInfo

Once a new bot is set up in WhatsApp, the app generates an API key that users can then use to connect their agent to the chat. As WABetaInfo explains it, “the exact steps depend on the platform, but most services have a field where users can paste” that API key, allowing them to start chatting with their third-party agent directly through WhatsApp.

Here’s WABetaInfo:

Once the agent is connected to a WhatsApp chat, users can open the new conversation to communicate with it. Users can send messages to the agent and receive responses directly within the app. Note that the agent can only read what the user shared in the chat with it. This means that the agent cannot access other conversations, contacts, or media. At the moment, it is only possible to chat with the agent in an individual chat. For this reason, users cannot add it to group chats and communities. In case the agent is an AI, WhatsApp notes that its responses may be inaccurate. As a result, users should always double-check anything the agent tells them.

The site notes that currently, select Android users have access to the new feature, but it is expected to roll out more broadly soon. WABetaInfo says WhatsApp’s implementation supports up to five agents per account, and lets users customize each one with a name and profile photo. However, chats with third-party agents are currently not end-to-end encrypted.

title: Samsung’s Privacy Display and TriFold merge in the Huawei Mate XT2
snippet: Huawei has unveiled its new Mate XT2 foldable, offering a tri-fold design that also implements Samsung’s Privacy Display feature from the Galaxy S26 Ultra. more…
fullText:
Huawei has unveiled its new Mate XT2 foldable, offering a tri-fold design that also implements Samsung’s Privacy Display feature from the Galaxy S26 Ultra.

The Privacy Display is Samsung’s big selling point on the Galaxy S26 Ultra, with the special tech adjusting the pixels in the display so that, when active, light is only emitted to where you’re the only one who can clearly see what’s showing on screen. It’s pretty awesome.

Galaxy S26 Ultra’s Privacy Display is the best truly-new smartphone feature in years [Gallery]

Samsung’s other big recent innovation in smartphones was the Galaxy Z TriFold, which launched with a 10-inch inner display that hides beneath a normal-ish smartphone screen. It’s also pretty awesome, though Samsung stopped selling the device pretty abruptly earlier this year.

Now, the Huawei Mate XT2 is here to merge the two together.

	

Huawei’s latest tri-fold device swaps out the previous design, which used a portion of the main display as an outer screen when folded, to match what Samsung’s Galaxy Z TriFold offered. The inward-facing design will likely better-protect the main display compared to the previous setup. 

The 10.2-inch display also has an optional privacy display, using tech that sounds similar to Samsung’s. As The Verge points out, this is only available on the 16GB/1TB version of the Mate XT2 and is an additional cost on top of that variant. And the Mate XT2 isn’t cheap, coming in at around $3,000 USD (¥19,999). This is likely a device that won’t see the light of day outside of China, as much as that purple colorway looks great. 

It’s powered by a Kirin 9050 Pro, HarmonyOS 7, measures 12.3mm when folded, weighs 299g, has stylus support, and also featured IP58/59 dust/water resistance. There are three cameras around back; 50MP main, 50MP 3.5x telephoto, and 40MP ultrawide, and there’s a 5,600 mAh battery.

title: Apple details how Apple Watch’s new Audio Intelligence features work in privacy paper
snippet: Apple is launching an all-new set of features called Audio Intelligence, starting with today’s new Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4. The company details how the new feature works, especially around privacy, in a new paper. more…
fullText:
Apple is launching an all-new set of features called Audio Intelligence, starting with today’s new Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4. The company details how the new feature works, especially around privacy, in a new paper. 

Audio Intelligence on Apple Watch covers four features, including Live Rewind and Siri Recap

“Audio Intelligence is a brand-new class of Apple Intelligence features that use the microphones of Apple Watch, the power of Apple silicon, and on-device and cloud-based AI models to help you detect sounds, identify music, and stay present and engaged — all while protecting your privacy at every step,” Apple explains. 

Audio Intelligence includes four specific features to start: Sound Recognition, automatic Music Recognition with Shazam, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. The company says that both Live Rewind and Siri Recap will arrive in beta with English support later this year, adding that “more details will be available at launch.”

Each Audio Intelligence feature is opt-in, Apple says. Live Rewind and Siri Recap also let you easily enable or disable the feature as needed.

Here’s more on Live Rewind from Apple:

Live Rewind only activates when you deliberately double-press the Digital Crown. It only shows the last 15 seconds of speech as a text snippet on your display. It doesn’t continue to transcribe in the background, nor does it save the text unless you choose to ask Siri about the content or save it to the Siri app. You can turn it on through the Watch app on iPhone — just open the Watch app, tap Siri, then tap Live Rewind and turn on “Double Click Digital Crown”.

And here’s more on Siri Recap from Apple:

Siri Recap runs only when you choose. You can turn on Siri Recap in the Watch app on iPhone. When you turn it on, you can set a schedule based on time and/or location (for example, “only at work” or “never at night”), or you can manually turn it on and off. Across all these options, you can always turn it on or off at any time from Control Center.

Audio Intelligence doesn’t attribute speech to speakers, and Siri Recap is designed to omit potentially harmful content and sensitive information. Live Rewind alerts nearby people with an audible chime and visual indicators, Apple says.

You can learn much more about the new features here.

How Audio Intelligence is designed to work with privacy in mind

If you want to really take a deep dive on privacy and the new features, Apple has published an 11-page privacy paper that goes even further.

Interestingly, Apple explains in the paper how Live Rewind works with privacy in mind:

Live Rewind Audio from the microphone flows into the audio buffer inside the Secure Exclave on the S11 chip. Old audio is continuously replaced by new audio, so audio doesn’t accumulate, and raw audio isn’t accessible outside this protected buffer.

And for the Siri Recap feature, here’s part of Apple’s explanation on how it works:

The S11 chip uses a lightweight AI model to determine whether speech is occurring nearby. This model doesn’t transcribe or record anything. It simply detects whether a conversation has started. If a conversation is detected, audio flows into a protected buffer inside the Secure Exclave on the S11 chip. It is isolated in hardware so that it is inaccessible to the user, the operating system, apps, and even Apple.

Again, you can read the full 11-page paper for yourself here.

title: Logitech launches $99 MX Keypad for coding and AI workflows
snippet: Programmable physical controls are becoming key to power user workflows, including agentic programming. Now Logitech is bringing to market a compact solution that fits on any desk. Logitech today announced the MX Keypad, a $99.99 accessory with nine customizable full-color LCD keys for launching commands, running macros, and accessing AI tools. more…
fullText:
Programmable physical controls are becoming key to power user workflows, including agentic programming. Now Logitech is bringing to market a compact solution that fits on any desk.

Logitech today announced the MX Keypad, a $99.99 accessory with nine customizable full-color LCD keys for launching commands, running macros, and accessing AI tools.

MX Keypad is half the price of Logitech’s MX Creative Console

If the hardware looks familiar, there’s a reason. Logitech’s MX Creative Console pairs an LCD keypad with a separate dialpad for adjusting settings and navigating creative apps.

MX Keypad offers the keypad experience without that additional controller, at half the Creative Console’s $199.99 list price.

The new product puts developers and AI workflows at the center of the pitch, although customization extends beyond coding apps.

Logi Options+ app lets you customize the experience

Through the free Logi Options+ app, users can assign shortcuts, saved prompts, scripts, and macros to individual keys. Two page buttons provide access to up to 15 pages, while app-aware profiles automatically switch layouts as you move between applications.

That means the same physical buttons can offer different actions in VS Code, Slack, Chrome, or another app. Logi Marketplace supplies plugins, profiles, and icon packs, and a built-in icon editor lets users personalize each key’s appearance.

You can use AI to program your AI keypad

My initial hands-on test consisted of connecting MX Keypad to my MacBook Air at my desk, then having Codex use computer use to program custom buttons in Logi Options+ based on how I use ChatGPT on Mac.

There’s something fitting about asking an AI coding agent to configure the physical controls you’ll use while working with AI. It also makes the appeal clear: putting the prompts and actions you repeatedly reach for onto dedicated, labeled buttons.

Logitech developed MX Keypad in collaboration with GitHub. The product includes GitHub Copilot integration in VS Code, plus three free months of Copilot Pro+ for both new and existing users, redeemable through Logi Options+.

Logitech also says community plugins for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex provide features such as agent status tracking and terminal controls. Developers who want to go further can build custom plugins using the Logi Actions SDK, which supports C# and Node.js.

The keypad connects over USB-C and requires macOS 13 or later, or Windows 10 or later. It measures approximately 3.6 by 3.1 inches and weighs 96 grams, making it a small addition next to a laptop or keyboard.

MX Keypad is available starting today, September 8, in Graphite and Pale Grey for $99.99.

title: Meta AI launches Muse personal agent, including a new mobile app for iPhone
snippet: Meta AI just launched a brand-new iPhone app called Muse from Meta. Similar to Grok Bot in presentation, Muse is a personal AI agent that handles tasks for you. more…
fullText:
Meta AI just launched a brand-new iPhone app called Muse from Meta. Similar to Grok Bot in presentation, Muse is a personal AI agent that handles tasks for you.

It follows the recent trend of AI companies creating personified characters to make AI agents more relatable and friendly, mimicking chat interfaces.

Muse is also available on the Mac through the web at muse.ai. The system lets you customize the agent name and avatar to personalize the experience.

Unlike other systems, Muse is free upfront with weekly limitations. Paying customers can unlock higher access.

You can learn more about the new Muse agent design here and security here. Muse is available for iPhone through the App Store.

The app is only available in the US for now, with more countries being added over time.

Last month, Meta AI also launched a more capable desktop app on the Mac.

Muse arrives the same month as Siri AI, which seems Apple upgrade its voice assistant for the chatbot era. While Siri AI is capable of taking some actions, it’s not a full blown agentic system yet like we’re seeing from OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceXAI, and Meta AI.

title: Arm’s new CPU cores and GPUs for Android chips promise ‘desktop-class’ games, more AI power
snippet: Arm has announced its new C2 CPUs for future Android chips as well as upgrades to its Mali GPUs that will take everything up a notch. more…
fullText:
Arm has announced its new C2 CPUs for future Android chips as well as upgrades to its Mali GPUs that will take everything up a notch.

Arm CPU designs are the backbone of many Android smartphone chips, including the likes of MediaTek flagships and Google’s Tensor as well. This week, Arm has announced its C2-Ultra and C2-Pro CPU cores, delivering a 15% boost to single-thread performance and 12% faster app launches, as well as local AI that’s built into the CPU itself instead of offloading to a dedicated NPU or TPU.

Arm claims:

Up to 1.7x performance improvement across the latest AI models

Up to 15 percent higher single-thread performance

15 percent faster web browsing

12 percent faster application launch

12 percent higher multi-thread performance at the cluster level, supporting parallel activity across retrieval, model preparation and application execution

But the more exciting announcement here is the GPU, with Arm’s new Mali G2-Ultra NX claiming to deliver “desktop-class” performance with the help of “AI-native graphics.” Arm says that this new GPU “integrates neural acceleration directly into the graphics pipeline, helping developers deliver richer, more responsive visual experiences within the mobile power envelope and bring neural graphics into production faster.”

	

The new GPU as a whole sees a 14% boost in performance, but also integrates Unreal Engine 5 “MegaLights” while also being able to generate intermediate frames for smooth gameplay or upscale low-res games. 

This could all show up in other form factors eventually, but it’s starting out in phones. Specifically, Xiaomi’s 18 Fold and its XRing O3 chip will be the first to integrate this new hardware, though games that take full advantage of it could be a ways out.

title: The Cadillac Lyriq EV is the first crack in GM’s CarPlay ban
snippet: General Motors first announced that it was ditching CarPlay in all future EVs back in 2023, subsequently issuing a series of ridiculous justifications – and at one point even implying it’s what Steve Jobs would have done. But it seems there is now one exception. Since that U-turn was reportedly based on customer feedback, perhaps GM is now rethinking its life decisions … more…
fullText:
General Motors first announced that it was ditching CarPlay in all future EVs back in 2023, subsequently issuing a series of ridiculous justifications – and at one point even implying it’s what Steve Jobs would have done.

But it seems there is now one exception. Since that U-turn was reportedly based on customer feedback, perhaps GM is now rethinking its life decisions …

Engadget spotted the CarBuzz report. 

The Cadillac configurator is up for several 2027 models, and we spotted that the Lyriq still shows CarPlay and Android Auto being standard. The Lyriq is Cadillac’s first all-electric vehicle and a tech-forward vehicle that we think is becoming one of the best luxury EVs available.

“Cadillac is continuing to evolve its infotainment strategy across the EV portfolio, based on customer feedback, while also prioritizing the native, in-vehicle experience,” a Cadillac representative told CarBuzz.

Read: We discovered customers weren’t going to buy a luxury EV without CarPlay.

Engadget also pointed to a handy workaround for owners of other GM models without CarPlay support.

For drivers of non-Lyriq GM EVs who prefer their phone mirroring application, the EV Play LT is a nifty workaround. Capable of providing wired and wireless phone mirroring for Chevy, GMC and Cadillac EVs, the EV Play LT is a third-party product that will deliver Apple CarPlay and Android Auto functionalities in infotainment systems without the popular phone mirroring apps. At $199.99 and with no subscription fees, the product might be just what the infotainment doctor ordered.

Is this the beginning of the end of GM’s attempt to wean us off CarPlay? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

title: OpenAI adds a prominent AI doomer to its board of directors
snippet: Paul Christiano, an influential AI researcher focused on alignment, is joining the OpenAI Foundation as a member of its board.
fullText:
Paul Christiano, an influential AI researcher focused on keeping AI systems aligned with human interests and under human control, is joining the OpenAI Foundation board, the frontier lab said Wednesday.

“I now believe there is a meaningful risk that rapid acceleration in AI capabilities leads to catastrophic and irreversible loss of control in the very near term,” Christiano wrote in a social media post. “I do not think that the AI industry in general, including OpenAI, is currently on track to reduce this risk to an acceptable level. I’m joining because I believe that if OpenAI rises to the occasion we could significantly reduce risk.”

Christiano wrote that using AI models to train subsequent AI systems could result in an explosion of capabilities that their creators can’t control.

He joins the board as OpenAI faces renewed scrutiny over its safety procedures, following a series of incidents in which AI agents broke out of restraints and penetrated outside computer systems without the knowledge of OpenAI’s researchers. On Tuesday, Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned his position to call attention to what he considers irresponsible AI development — and it seems to have worked.

Christiano will join the board’s Safety and Security Committee, led by Carnegie Mellon University professor Zico Kolter. The committee has the final say on whether OpenAI releases new models, like Astra, which was deployed last week. Kolter has not commented publicly on the recent security incidents. OpenAI has not responded to TechCrunch’s request for Kolter’s perspective on the company’s approach to safety following those incidents.

Christiano is one of the people behind reinforcement learning (RL) from human feedback, a key technique for training large language models that he developed while working at OpenAI. He left the lab in 2021, subsequently founding the Alignment Research Center to focus on how to determine if an AI model could threaten its human creators.

“We currently train our AI agents with RL to get as much reward as they can,” he wrote Wednesday. “It has long seemed theoretically possible that this could motivate AI agents to undermine human control, seek power and resources, and cover up their tracks in pursuit of misaligned goals correlated with reward. Public evidence from recent incidents suggests that this is not just a theoretical possibility.”

Sometime in 2024, Christiano became affiliated with the U.S. government’s AI Safety Institute, which later became the Center for AI Standards and Innovation. There, he plays a role in the U.S. government’s largely hidden effort to evaluate frontier AI models before their release.

According to the frontier lab’s announcement, Christiano will continue advising the government while serving in his new role as a board member, but will recuse himself from OpenAI matters and model evaluations. However, that will hardly quell widespread concerns about the AI industry’s influence over policymaking.

title: Massachusetts hits data centers with new clean power rules
snippet: Massachusetts has become the third state in as many months to slap new restrictions on data center development.
fullText:
Massachusetts became the latest state to force data centers to bring their own power, but this time there’s a twist. A new state mandate would require developers building data centers larger than 25 megawatts to provide clean power or pay into a ratepayer protection fund.

Gov. Maura Healey’s executive order is the latest example of states turning against data centers. Just a few years ago, tech companies and data center developers were showered with incentives to locate facilities in a particular state. Now they’re fighting a groundswell of public opposition as politicians seek to show voters they’re addressing their concerns.

Under Healey’s order, data centers larger than 25 megawatts of peak demand will have to bring their own power and guarantee that it adheres to the state’s clean energy requirements. Healey would prefer that they generate the clean power on-site, too. If not, they’ll need to fund the construction of new generation nearby or pay into a ratepayer protection fund.

Massachusetts is also directing communities to “avoid signing non-disclosure agreements,” according to the executive order. To give regulators time to implement the new restrictions, the governor is pausing applications for a data center sales tax exemption that went into effect last month.

Healey said data centers must meet the Massachusetts clean energy standard enshrined in state law, although it comes with some added strength. The state’s clean energy standard dictates that industry only generate a portion of their power using approved sources like wind, solar, and hydro. In 2030, for example, those sources must contribute at least 40% of the total. The amount varies by year, and it ratchets up over time. But the governor’s office clarified that data centers will be required to meet 100% of its electricity demand with clean energy generation.

With the new restrictions, Massachusetts becomes the third state in as many months to rein in data center development.

In August, Texas governor Greg Abbott announced that all new data centers in the state would need to submit to audits by the public utility commission and the grid operator, ERCOT. In July, New York’s governor stopped construction of new data centers 50 megawatts or larger. 

With public sentiment shifting against data centers, the tech industry is starting to push back. Pro-AI super PAC Leading the Future — which is funded by Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz, and Greg Brockman — is buying ads that seek to sway voters in battleground states ahead of midterm elections.

Update: This article was updated with information from the Massachusetts governor’s office that clarified the executive order will require data centers to meet 100% of its electricity demand with clean energy generation.

title: Apple Watch’s new AI features are normalizing the idea that technology is always listening
snippet: Apple says its new watches won’t save raw audio, but features that can transcribe recent speech and summarize ambient conversations raise new questions about consent, privacy, and how people behave when they know they could always be recorded.
fullText:
Apple is trying to get consumers to accept, and even welcome, a new reality: Your tech is always listening.

At Wednesday’s Surprise and Shine event, where the company introduced its new hardware lineup, the real surprise turned out not to be the foldable iPhone, but how the privacy-sensitive tech giant has decided its watches will now be able to process live audio and transcribe what was said.

Does this mean you’re always being recorded if the person you’re interacting with is wearing an Apple Watch? Not exactly — though it may make some people uncomfortable regardless. 

It also raises the question of whether consumers actually want this technology, or if Apple forged ahead in this area because it was afraid that another company, such as OpenAI, would soon introduce a competitive AI device of its own.

Today, a number of startups are acting on the belief that AI-powered transcription is a key consumer use case for AI. So far, this has often involved transcribing meeting notes or recording lectures or interviews. Some companies, like the AI pendant Friend and Amazon’s Bee, ventured into other areas, too, with always-available AI companions that can help you remember your day by passively taking notes.

Apple decided to go a slightly different route. With its new watches’ “Audio Intelligence,” “Live Rewind,” and “Siri Recap” features, the company is straddling the line between accessibility and utility on one side and what starts to feel like invasive technology on the other.

On its own, Audio Intelligence seems to be a useful feature for the deaf or hard of hearing, as it can alert Apple Watch wearers to sounds like sirens, alarms, doorbells, babies crying, and more, using on-device AI. This can work even when the wearer’s iPhone is not with them and, in some cases, could provide life-saving assistance, such as when a fire alarm or carbon-monoxide detector goes off. It’s doubtful anyone would take issue with this type of audio AI.

Image Credits:Apple

However, Live Rewind and Siri Recap move out of the assistive tech space and into a murkier area.

While Apple’s data protections may make these features more palatable to some, there’s still the possibility that normalizing listening technology may not be the best move for a privacy-conscious company. This is especially true given the broader consumer backlash against surveillance technology like Flock cameras, AI data centers, and AI apps in general.

For starters, the Live Rewind AI feature lets you go back in time 15 seconds and transcribe what was just said by double-pressing the watch’s Digital Crown. This transcription can then be saved to Apple’s new stand-alone Siri app so you can revisit the information later.

Image Credits:Apple

Apple suggests this could be used to remember things like a “book recommendation, a colleague’s brilliant idea, or something you didn’t hear the first time,” but it also means that you can essentially catch anyone saying something they didn’t necessarily mean to have recorded and make a note of it.

This has implications around consent, not only from an ethical standpoint but from a legal one as well. AI device maker Plaud, for instance, advises customers to obtain legally required consent before recording. Amazon Bee’s terms of service remind users that they’re solely responsible for complying with the law around minors’ data privacy, not Amazon.

Since Apple isn’t saving audio, it’s unclear how the court system might handle these new, text-only transcripts. It’s possible the notes could be introduced as evidence in court, but their lack of audio could make them harder to authenticate or verify. Plus, the evidentiary rules around their use will also likely vary by state. 

Beyond the legal issues, the idea that someone can always record from their watch has cultural implications.

Already, recording devices have impacted the way people behave in real life, studies have shown, as has social media and data surveillance culture. Knowing you could be recorded at any time has a dampening effect on how you interact with others and engage in self-expression.

Image Credits:Apple

However, recording a photo or video still requires a fairly obvious move on the recorder’s part: You have to hold up your phone and face it toward the action. Snapping up a bit of audio to turn into a transcript just by pressing the watch’s Digital Crown is arguably a much subtler gesture, even though it comes with an audible chime and full-screen animation of a microphone, Apple says.

Another new Apple Watch feature, “Siri Recap,” uses ambient listening to “take high-level notes” of your conversations, which can be reviewed in the Siri iOS app. These notes will automatically generate a title, summary, and key points based on what was recorded and summarized by AI. They will not be exact transcripts.

Apple suggests this could make sense for recording meeting takeaways or key info from a parent-teacher conference, for instance. 

The company also tried to assure users that it has approached these listening features with respect for user privacy.

Apple notes that Siri Recap doesn’t default to always being on like some other AI wearables are. Instead, you can choose when it’s enabled, like only at work or only during the day. Plus, you can turn the feature off and on at any time from the Control Center.

Notably, Apple points out that it does not create or store audio recordings and that the raw audio isn’t accessible, even to Apple. It also doesn’t identify or attribute the speakers, and it protects the generated transcripts and recaps with end-to-end encryption.

Whether that’s enough for consumers not to feel like the feature is creepy is another matter. Either Apple has found the right balance between utility and privacy, or it’s about to see some consumer backlash.

title: There are new shiny iPhones, so Apple is making you pay more for older models
snippet: Apple is raising the price of its existing iPhone models by $100, including iPhone 16, iPhone 17, and iPhone Air.
fullText:
Apple, at its Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday, unveiled its new iPhone 18 and its first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo. But amid all the attention on Apple’s newest and most expensive devices, there’s another change: Apple is raising the price of its existing iPhone models by $100.

Starting today, customers will notice a price hike for existing models on Apple’s online store, including starting prices for iPhone 16 at $799, iPhone 17e at $699, iPhone 17 at $899, and iPhone Air at $1,099. 

The price increases are even steeper in some international markets. In India, for example, prices have reportedly risen by around 20.5%. The company also discontinued the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max.

The strategy is an unusual one for Apple. Traditionally, the arrival of a new generation of iPhones means older models become cheaper.

However, the price hike wasn’t entirely unexpected. Speculation had been building that Apple could raise prices as it introduced its next-generation iPhones. One of the biggest pressures is a global shortage of memory and storage chips. Demand for those components has surged as AI companies and cloud providers build out increasingly massive data centers.

In a June interview with The Wall Street Journal, former Apple CEO Tim Cook acknowledged that rising component costs could eventually force the company to rethink its pricing strategy. He said Apple could no longer fully absorb the rising costs of memory and storage chips.

About a week after those comments, the company raised prices across its Mac and iPad lineups.

Another reason Apple may consider increasing iPhone prices is to remain competitive with rising prices from rivals like Samsung and Google. Additionally, Apple might feel that its new Upgrade program, which allows customers to spread the cost of an iPhone through manageable monthly payments, could cushion the impact of a price hike, making it less noticeable to consumers.

title: Apple Is Actually Talking About AI Now — a Lot
snippet: New CEO John Ternus says you already have your personal AI device. It’s called an iPhone.
fullText:
It wasn’t that long ago that I wrote about how Apple’s reserved AI strategy is probably its best yet. By not hemorrhaging money on AI features and tools and by focusing on hardware rather than going all-in on AI, Apple positioned itself to come out ahead while its competitors beat and batter themselves to out-innovate each other in AI.

Yeah, that’s out the window now.

During its September “Surprise and shine” event on Wednesday at Apple Park in Cupertino, California, the company opened with a discussion of AI. Not merely “intelligence” or even “Apple Intelligence,” but artificial intelligence specifically. Clearly, Apple is not timid about tying AI use to its hardware improvements. Here are the AI and Siri AI features Apple went all-in on during the event. 

Welcome to the vanguard of consumer AI, Apple.

AI as core architecture 

New Apple CEO John Ternus doubled down on the company’s seemingly new AI strategy. “As we look ahead, we see a future filled with enormous discovery and transformation,” he said. “AI makes entirely new kinds of experiences possible. And AI can become even more useful when it brings together your life with the apps, services and products you use every day. And this means the product at the center of your experiences becomes even more essential.”

That product at the center of your AI universe? Well, it’s an iPhone.

He called the iPhone an “intelligent personal hub,” framing it as an intersection of advanced AI capabilities and an understanding of your personal context. The system will use that context, including your calendars, contacts, routines, messages and app activity, to provide more relevant assistance to you as you go through your day. 

Apple acknowledged that personalization and customization come with data privacy concerns. 

During the event, Ternus emphasized that Apple Intelligence defaults to on-device processing, so your data stays with you rather than some far-off server. When extra power and capability are required, your requests extend to Private Cloud Compute, with privacy protections that ensure no one (including Apple) can access your personal data. 

AI on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max

According to Lilian Rincon, Apple VP of AI product marketing, the new iPhone 18 Pro “is built to take full advantage of all the capabilities of Apple Intelligence.” With it, you’ll get access to the latest Apple Foundation Models and, perhaps most notably, the most advanced Siri AI capabilities to date. 

The new version of Siri “goes further than ever before” by combining personal context awareness, on-screen and in-app action, and a dedicated Siri app that you can customize. On your device, Siri can cross-reference, take action and synthesize your information across 300,000 native and third-party apps, like Mail, Messages, WhatsApp, Outlook and beyond. For instance, Siri can combine details from your emails and texts to create a summary of what you need to do to prepare for an upcoming family visit. 

Visual intelligence is also expanding, as Siri can “see what you see.” 

Using the camera or display, you can have Siri see what’s in front of you to ask questions or execute actions. With this feature, you could upload a photo and ask Siri which produce is best for a recipe your mom sent you via email. Siri can reference the email, your photo and its real-world knowledge to give you an answer and then add the ingredients to your grocery list in a separate app. (I wouldn’t be surprised if this feature eventually comes to AirPods or smart glasses.) 

The iPhone 18 Pro line also comes with a new dedicated Siri app right on the home screen, featuring customization options such as Expressive Voices. Powered by a new on-device model, you can customize Siri’s voice pacing and expressivity across the Siri app, Safari and Maps. Want more inflection in Siri’s audio? You can simply adjust it on a sliding scale. 

Apple appears to be all-in on integrating Apple Intelligence into every part of the iPhone, from writing and notifications to surfacing important information from phone calls and taking or editing photos. 

Powered by a new on-device model, you can customize Siri’s voice pacing and expressivity.Screenshot by CNET/Apple

Beyond the iPhone

Apple Intelligence is also coming baked into other hardware beyond the iPhone. 

The new AirPods 5 let you access Siri hands-free, giving you access to all of Siri’s knowledge and capabilities without touching the device. AirPods 5 also come with built-in active noise cancellation and Live Translation to translate between different languages in real-time conversations.

The latest Apple Watch (Series 12 and Ultra 4) is rolling out with an Audio Intelligence feature that recaps conversations for you, along with a slew of AI health features to deliver a deeper understanding of your health metrics. Apple Intelligence brings summaries of your health trends, recommendations for recovery and a revamped health app – all of which you can read about in depth here. 

Expanded language support

Apple Intelligence comes out in 16 supported languages with OS releases coming this month, including English, French, Spanish, German, Italian and Chinese (though Apple Intelligence will not be available in China). 

Siri AI beta launches in English, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish coming in October.

title: TrendForce: Apple produced 52 million iPhones in Q2 as global smartphone market declined
snippet: A new TrendForce report shows that Apple saw a 14% year-over-year increase in smartphone production during Q2 2026, reaching a 19% share of global production, second only to Samsung. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A new TrendForce report shows that Apple saw a 14% year-over-year increase in smartphone production during Q2 2026, reaching a 19% share of global production, second only to Samsung. Here are the details.

Market-wide decline less steep than previously predicted

In a report published today, TrendForce says Apple produced approximately 52 million iPhone units during Q2 2026, a 14% increase from the year-ago period.

Global smartphone production for the period, however, dropped 8% year over year to 275 million units. The decline was “narrower than previously forecast, resulting in better-than-expected overall performance,” says TrendForce.

In light of the new numbers, TrendForce revised its 2026 forecast, raising its global smartphone production estimate to 1.07 billion units, up from 1.05 billion in a previous report. If confirmed, that would represent a 14% year-over-year decline, compared with the 16% drop previously forecast.

Apple’s performance was second only to Samsung, which produced 62 million smartphones during Q2 2026, a 7% year-over-year increase, accounting for 23% of global production.

After Apple, Oppo came in third with 30 million units and an 11% share (down 17% year over year), followed by Xiaomi with 29 million units and 10% share (-32%), vivo with 21 million units and 8% share (-18%), and Transsion with 20 million units and 7% share (-27%).

Here’s TrendForce on Apple’s numbers:

Growth was primarily driven by the effective pricing strategy of the iPhone 17 series, which supported strong sales performance through the first three quarters.

The report added that “price increases for the upcoming iPhone 18 series appear inevitable, making their potential impact on sales momentum a key factor to watch.”

Finally, TrendForce also noted that its upward revision for the whole of 2026 reflects consumers buying smartphones earlier than planned and manufacturers reversing some of their previous aggressive production cuts, rather than an increase in underlying demand.

title: AI research startup Listen Labs scrubbed a $1.5B funding round for Salesforce talks
snippet: Listen Labs walked away from a signed Series C term sheet from Menlo Ventures, sources say.
fullText:
Listen Labs, a market research startup that uses voice AI to conduct customer interviews, recently signed a term sheet for a $125 million Series C at a $1.5 billion valuation, with Menlo Ventures set to lead the round, according to several people with knowledge of the matter.

But that round never closed, the people said. Listen Labs walked away from the signed term sheet, a rare occurrence in the venture world and one that is generally frowned upon, according to VCs.

The financing likely collapsed because of acquisition talks with Salesforce. The CRM giant has recently held talks to buy Listen Labs for around $2 billion, Business Insider reported. The discussions are not finalized, however, and may not result in a deal, the outlet notes.

Listen Labs is one of the leading startups in the rapidly growing field of automating customer research with AI. The three-year-old startup has about $30 million in annualized revenue, about three times more than Simile, a competing startup that predicts human behavior, according to two people familiar with the companies’ financials. In late July, Simile announced that it had closed a $200 million Series B at a $2 billion valuation led by Greenoaks — likely setting a new valuation benchmark for Listen Labs, one person said.

If talks with Salesforce collapse, several VCs told TechCrunch that they expect Listen Labs to return to market and target a valuation of $2 billion or higher.

While acquiring Listen Labs could strengthen Salesforce’s AI capabilities by using the startup’s AI to help predict customer needs, the CRM giant may ultimately decide that paying a 67 times revenue multiple is too steep a valuation, according to a person with experience negotiating exits to Salesforce.

Listen Labs, Salesforce, Menlo Ventures, and Simile did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Listen Labs was co-founded in 2023 by Florian Jüngermann, a former German national champion in competitive computer programming, and Alfred Wahlforss, who previously founded a staffing startup called Bemlo. The two met while pursuing master’s degrees at Harvard.

Listen Labs’ AI develops survey questions and interviews customers over audio or video. The resulting conversations are then packaged into reports and PowerPoint presentations, similar to those traditionally produced by human market researchers.

Fortune 500 companies rely on this type of research to gauge customer needs and satisfaction with their brands and products, but traditional market research is expensive and can take weeks to complete.

Listen Labs’ technology helps reduce the time and cost of these projects, enabling companies to quickly understand how customers are reacting to product changes and iterate on them more efficiently.

The startup’s customers include Microsoft, Canva, Anthropic, and Sweetgreen. Listen Labs and Simile aren’t the only startups using AI to disrupt the customer research market.

Besides Simile, competitors in the space include Outset, Keplar, and Aaru. While some platforms automate interviews with real humans, others startups — like Aaru and Simile — take a synthetic approach, using AI to simulate human behavior and predict responses without interviewing anyone at all.

Listen Labs was previously valued at $500 million when it announced a $69 million Series B round in late January led by Ribbit Capital, with participation from returning backers Sequoia, Conviction, and Pear VC.

title: Apple CEO John Ternus says the best AI device is still the iPhone
snippet: The company also argued that its on-device models offer consumers more privacy.
fullText:
Apple’s new CEO, John Ternus, used the opening of the company’s Surprise and Shine event Wednesday to make its AI strategy clear: The iPhone is already the best AI device out there, and Apple cares more about data privacy than its rivals.

The comments come as Ternus takes the reins at Apple from Tim Cook, who is now executive chairman, and offer a clear picture of how the company plans to compete in the AI era. Instead of building new hardware for AI, Apple wants to make the iPhone the central way consumers interact with the new technology.

During his introduction at the Cupertino event, Ternus described the ideal AI device as an “intelligent personal hub.” He said such a hub would have a broad understanding of a user’s personal context, always be with them, and have both a powerful processor capable of running AI models on-device and an internet connection to access models in the cloud.

The device would also have a large display, high-quality cameras, and microphones so it could see and hear the world around it, along with long battery life, Ternus continued.

Plus, “you’d want it to be super easy to use without a big learning curve. And finally, you’d want it to work seamlessly with your other devices, apps, and services, so it feels like one integrated experience,” he said.

“In other words, you would arrive at something remarkably familiar, because there’s no product in the world better designed to be your intelligent personal hub than iPhone,” Ternus said. 

Ternus also emphasized how Apple cares more about data privacy, adding that “others see [users’ personal] data as something to collect and store.” It was one of the sharper statements Apple has made about how it intends to differentiate its AI platform from the competition.

“Honestly, trust only goes so far when your data is no longer yours to control; that’s why Apple Intelligence runs on device whenever it can,” Ternus concluded.

title: iPadOS 27 launches on September 14, here are the compatible devices
snippet: During its “Surprise and Shine” event today, Apple confirmed that iPadOS 27 will be released in just a few days, on September 14. Here are the compatible devices. more…
fullText:
During its “Surprise and Shine” event today, Apple confirmed that iPadOS 27 will be released in just a few days, on September 14. Here are the compatible devices.

iPadOS 27 to be released on September 14

Apple today announced the iPhone Duo, the company’s first foldable iPhone, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro, and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

In addition to the new hardware, Apple also confirmed the release date of iPadOS 27, which was first announced during WWDC26.

Like iOS 27, iPadOS 27’s headlining feature is the new Siri AI, powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Apple Foundation Models, as well as Apple’s partnership with Google and its Gemini models.

The revamped assistant is designed to offer an experience closer to modern LLMs, using the user’s personal context to provide more relevant and in-depth answers. Siri can also search the web for information and use what it finds to generate complete, useful responses.

iPadOS 27 also introduces welcome adjustments to the Liquid Glass look, brings performance improvements to several system apps, and more.

title: Apple unveils Watch Series 12 and Watch Ultra 4 with an AI upgrade that can recap your day
snippet: Most notably, Apple is taking aim at the growing wave of AI wearables with new "Audio Intelligence" features that let you rewind moments and remember details from daily conversations.
fullText:
Apple on Wednesday unveiled the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 at its Surprise and Shine event in Cupertino. While the smartwatches aren’t getting a major hardware makeover, they are getting some significant software updates.

Most notably, Apple is taking aim at the growing wave of AI wearables with new “Audio Intelligence” features that let you rewind moments and remember details from daily conversations. 

The smartwatches are launching with “Live Rewind,” a feature Apple describes as letting you go back up to 15 seconds. A double press of the Digital Crown shows the previous 15 seconds of a conversation as a text snippet. You can ask Siri about the content of that transcript, or save it to the new Siri app to revisit later.

Image Credits:Apple

There’s a “Siri Recap” feature that’s designed to help you remember key moments from daily conversations. It uses ambient listening to take high-level notes of your conversations, like takeaways from a team meeting or a parent-teacher conference. When Siri Recap is turned on, after a conversation, Apple Intelligence automatically generates a title and key points in the new Siri app. 

A new “Sound Recognition” feature will be able to listen for sounds like sirens, alarms, doorbells, a baby crying, and more for people who are hard of hearing. 

Apple says these audio intelligence features do not create or store audio recordings.

Both of the new smartwatches feature a health-sensing system with an increased electrode surface area for better skin contact during ECG readings. For improved optical sensing, redesigned photodiodes are arranged in a ring to capture light more efficiently. There are also more power-efficient green LEDs that enable accurate heart-rate measurements throughout the day, even during motion.

The new health-sensing system delivers higher frequency continuous heart rate data, which is a key indicator of your overall health. Background heart rate readings are now taken every five seconds all day long, even while you’re on the go. That’s 60x more frequent than before.

Image Credits:Apple

The smartwatches are taking a page from smart rings with new readiness scores that analyze your recent activity, vitals, and sleep each morning, distilling it all into a single score that indicates how prepared your body is to take on the day.

There’s also a new “Health Age” feature that lets users see how their key health metrics compare with their actual age, based on data from their watch, including VO2 max, sleep, and more.

The Apple Watch Series 12 starts at $399, while the Apple Watch Ultra 4 costs $499.

fullText:
Today, Volvo announced it was giving its hybrid XC40 a major facelift. When it arrives at dealerships early next year, the new XC40 will have updated exterior styling, a gut-renovated interior featuring Google’s Gemini AI assistant, enlarged infotainment screen, and a new sensor-and-software safety suite.

As a hybrid, the XC40 serves as a bridge for customers who want better gas mileage but aren’t ready for the pure EV lifestyle. Volvo itself needs that bridge, after backing down from its pledge to sell only EVs by 2030. That said, the automaker didn’t divulge any details about the powertrain, engine options, electric motor, range, or battery capacity for the XC40 — so we’ll have to wait and see whether this SUV can sufficiently compete in an increasingly cutthroat hybrid market.

On the surface, we’ve got a new take on Volvo’s signature “Thor’s Hammer” LED headlights, as well as an updated front grille, bumper, hood and front wings. Same goes for the rear: new lighting, new bumper, and an upgraded tailgate. Additionally, the XC40 is getting a trio of diamond-cut wheel options, available in 18-, 19-, and 20-inch sizes.

1/7

But the interior is where the meat of Volvo’s improvements comes through. The screen has been bumped up to a higher resolution and a larger, 11.2-inch size. It will run Volvo’s latest user interface, which the automaker designed for faster navigation with fewer taps. Google’s Gemini serves as the voice assistant, using its big AI brain to plan routes, find specific locations and detours, and manage messages. The XC40 rounds it out with an improved wireless phone charger and smart storage solutions.

What about safety? This is a Volvo after all, the automaker most committed to Safety (at least according to its well-cultivated reputation). Don’t worry, the XC40 ups the ante in that department with a new software and sensor platform that’s designed to provide real-time collision avoidance, automated emergency steering, and automatic emergency braking.

The sensor upgrade includes new front and corner radars, a new front camera, new rear corner radars, 12 new ultrasonic sensors, and new parking cameras. Cloaked in this new sensor suite, the XC40 is getting a host of new safety capabilities, including new door opening alerts that warn occupants before dooring passing cyclists, lane change assist and smoother lane following support on long drives, and an optional 3D/360-degree camera to simplify low-speed maneuvering and parking.

1/4

The ultimate goal is to build a better XC40 — one that’s safer and more capable, which hopefully translates to better sales numbers and a long, continuous shelf life for Volvo’s tiny SUV.

“By enhancing the XC40’s design, technology and safety features, we’ve created the best version of the XC40 yet,” says Akhil Krishnan, Interim Lead for the 30 and 40 Series at Volvo Cars, in a statement. “This already popular model is now set to continue being one of our best-selling cars for years to come.”

Images by Volvo

Correction September 10th: A previous version of this story described the new XC40 as a plug-in hybrid. It is a mild hybrid.

title: All iPhones — Not Just the Pro Models — Now Cost $100 More
snippet: RAMageddon comes for the iPhone.
fullText:
Apple has raised the prices of all iPhone models by $100. The price hike affects not just the new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max models – announced at Wednesday’s live “Surprise and Shine” event — but also last year’s iPhone 17, iPhone 17E and iPhone Air, as well as the iPhone 16.

The iPhone 17 now starts at $929, the highest ever starting price for Apple’s base iPhone model. The entry-level iPhone 17E now starts at $699, while the iPhone Air starts at $1,099. The iPhone 16 is now back to $829 — the same price it had when it debuted in 2024. 

While a price hike was expected for the newest iPhone models, the increase for older models is unprecedented. In previous years, older iPhones in the lineup either received a discount or maintained their original price.

Apple already raised the prices of several products in June, including Macs, iPads and HomePods, due to the global RAM shortage. Former Apple CEO Tim Cook called the price hikes “unavoidable,” citing a “100-year flood on the memory pricing.” RAMageddon caused companies, including Samsung and Google, to increase the cost of their new phones this year, but Apple spared the iPhone until Wednesday.

The cheapest new iPhone model, the iPhone 18 Pro, starts at $1,199; the most expensive new model is the $1,999 iPhone Duo. A base-model iPhone 18 wasn’t announced this week, but is expected to debut next spring.

title: Apple launches iPhone 18 Pro with upgraded camera
snippet: Apple's new iPhone 18 Pro lineup upgrades the camera and comes in burgundy.
fullText:
Apple launched its latest Pro phones, the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone 18 Pro Max, today at its fall Surprise and Shine iPhone event. While the design of the phones remains the same as the earlier model, the upgraded cameras are the highlight of the new devices.

The new Pro series camera features a 48-megapixel camera with variable aperture, made with six thin blades. This system will likely improve low-light photograph quality and speed. There are also new pro controls in the camera software, including white balance, shutter speed, aperture, and histogram. And new photographic styles with texture and grain controls might be the answer to the new “looks” feature on the Pixel 11 series for a more retro style.

The new camera can record 4K videos in Dolby HDR Vision and can apply cinematic effects after shooting the footage.

The new Pro devices also have a smaller dynamic island on the front of the device, which now allows you to track three live activities instead of two.

Both phones are powered by Apple’s latest A20 Pro silicon and feature a newly designed vapor chamber for improved cooling. The company has also improved the battery with a better design. Apple said the iPhone 18 Pro supports video playback of 36 hours, and the 18 Pro Max has 45 hours of playback capacity.

The company showed off the new Siri AI with contextual on-screen intelligence. It said the new Siri AI will support English in beta at launch with the iOS 27 rollout this month, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish support coming in October.

The new devices will also get the iPhone handoff feature with iOS 27 that allows you to use two iPhones with one eSIM and switch back and forth between them. 

The company is debuting a striking new burgundy color, replacing the orange from the previous lineup.

The iPhone 18 Pro costs $1,199, and the 18 Pro Max costs $1,299, which is $100 more than last year’s devices. People can preorder the devices on Saturday, and the devices will be available on September 18.

title: Apple has a new way to prove your iPhone photos aren’t AI slop
snippet: Apple introduced Apple Reference Image to help users determine whether photos have been edited, including alterations made by AI.
fullText:
Image Credits:Apple	

	

						

11:08 AM PDT · September 9, 2026

											

			

In a world awash in AI slop, Apple wants you to trust what gets captured on its iPhones.

The company announced Wednesday during its Surprise and Shine event that it is introducing Apple Reference Image, a feature it says can prove whether an image taken with the iPhone 18 Pro is authentic. 

“This is vital for photojournalists and photographers,” the company said.

When a photo is taken, the main camera sensor also captures signed sensor data, which Apple’s Private Cloud Compute service then turns into an “unalterable image” viewable in the Photos app. The reference image can then be compared with other versions of the photo to determine whether any changes have been made. Apple likens the reference image to a “digital negative.”

While reference images will initially be viewable only in the Photos app, the company is making APIs available to developers so they can integrate the feature into their own apps.

Apple also said it will support the SynthID standard to help people determine whether images were created or altered with AI.

Apple Reference Image is one of several new features and upgrades to the company’s hardware and software that is focused on the camera. 

The company said the iPhone 18 Pro includes its biggest camera improvement in years. One upgrade that will surely get the attention of photographers is the variable aperture on the new 48 megapixel fusion main camera. The aperture is what controls how much light enters the lens. This new main camera has a variable aperture, which means users have more control over the amount of light coming in and ultimately what the final image looks like. It should be especially helpful for those who like to take photos at night.  

To achieve this, Apple said it developed a system of six laser-cut blades, each thinner than a human hair and made from a specialized polymer composite, a new rotor mechanism to control movements, and a custom-designed lens.

title: Apple’s latest acquisition is about technology that sounds futuristic
snippet: EU filings revealed today that Apple has acquired a company called Sonera, makers of wearable-centered technology that sounds like it’s from the future. more…
fullText:
EU filings revealed today that Apple has acquired a company called Sonera, makers of wearable-centered technology that sounds like it’s from the future.

Apple acquires Sonera, whose technology reads brain activity by measuring magnetic fields

Apple is a secretive company that often doesn’t disclose its acquisitions. But under the EU’s Digital Markets Act, certain acquisitions have to be disclosed publicly on the EU’s website.

Today the latest addition to that site is Sonera, a company that “is developing a chip-based magnetic sensor.”

Here are more details, per a Sonera press release from 2023:

Sonera has developed a new sensing modality that non-invasively measures magnetic fields generated by the body, in contrast with the electrical sensing techniques commonly used today. This proprietary technology holds the key to making brain activity as easy to measure as heart rate, temperature, and other physiological signals, and enabling data-backed insights related to movement, health, thoughts, and emotions.

The press release, first discovered by MacRumors, mentions an S1 chip which could “enable an entirely new class of consumer wearables and experiences based on muscle activity.” 

Sonera’s proprietary approach “measures magnetic fields produced by the electrical currents from neural activity” and thus bypasses the need for direct skin contact.

It’s unclear how much progress Sonera has been able to make since that 2023 press release. But clearly, Apple found something of value in their technology.

The ability to read brain activity through measuring magnetic fields sounds like it could be the premise for a new Apple TV sci-fi series. But it’s easy to see lots of potential as Apple pushes further into wearables, and enhances its wearable products with AI.

title: NASA and IBM Launch Open-Source AI Model for Future Moon Explorations
snippet: One small step for AI, one giant leap for mankind.
fullText:
The NASA‑IBM Lunar Foundation Model is one of the first of its kind: a publicly available AI model created to support exploration of the moon under NASA’s Artemis program.   

Launched on Thursday and now available on the collaborative, open-source AI platform Hugging Face, the model was trained on decades of lunar observation data selected by IBM and NASA researchers to provide insights to advance human presence on the moon, according to a press release. 

IBM and NASA have worked together for over 60 years, since they first collaborated to put the first man on the moon.

A new phase for moon exploration

In the past, scientists had to manually examine maps and images collected by different instruments that had been analyzing the moon for decades. Or they used low-resolution machine learning models designed only for a specific task.

This infographic shows how the NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model helps analyze widespread lunar imagery and data.IBM

The NASA‑IBM Lunar Foundation Model not only saves researchers time by identifying data patterns at scale and across different instruments but, according to the press release, also outperforms widely used methods by up to 23% in identifying the moon’s key geographic features. This includes craters, volcanic formations and potential ice deposits, all of which provide crucial information for future Artemis moon explorations. 

Shining light on the first lunar dataset of its kind

In addition to the foundation AI model, IBM and NASA scientists also built what they’re calling the first open-source lunar dataset of its kind, bringing together tens of thousands of maps and images collected by nine instruments across four moon missions. 

The NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model uses multiple lunar data inputs to identify areas on the moon that may contain ice.IBM

Campbell Watson, senior research manager at IBM Research, told CNET in an email that by making the model and the dataset publicly available, IBM and NASA want to provide the global scientific community with a shared foundation that researchers can adapt and apply to new questions about the moon. 

“This work builds on decades of publicly released lunar data collected across multiple missions, so open-sourcing the model continues that tradition of broad scientific access and collaboration,” Watson said.

The NASA‑IBM Lunar Foundation Model isn’t the only one of NASA and IBM’s open-source AI models on Hugging Face. It also hosts the Prithvi family of models for weather, climate and earth observation.

The NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model can analyze lunar imagery to automatically identify craters on the moon.IBM

Researchers can build on the NASA‑IBM model to make new discoveries, rather than creating an AI model from scratch each time.

Last week Sonos unveiled several new features coming to its app soon, and now the first of those upgrades are here in the ‘Sonos 27’ app update. Here are the details.

Following the example of iOS 27 and others, Sonos is moving to a ‘Sonos 27’ naming scheme for its software platform.

Headphone Linking (Early Access): “Ace Ultra headphones connects to your Sonos system, letting listeners push and pull sound between nearby speakers and their ears without a phone as the middleman.”

Sonos 27mcp (Early Access): ”Connect AI assistants including ChatGPT and Claude to Sonos giving you more choice, rather than locking listeners into a single assistant.”

Sonos has also highlighted two more features coming soon:

Sonos 27voice (Later this Fall): “Sonos’ own music-focused assistant, reinforcing that no single AI needs to own the home and building around consumer choice.”

Sonos Custom Agents (2027): “Lets people create their own agents within the system, each with its own model, persona and voice.”

Sonos caused quite a stir a few years ago when it launched a major new app redesign. Today’s new navigation revamp appears a much smaller change, so hopefully it won’t create any controversy.

title: Ugreen’s ‘HomeAgent’ is a local AI smart home ecosystem for its new line of cameras, more
snippet: Ugreen might be most well-known for its chargers and device accessories, but its recent announcement might push it deeper into the smart home space. The company announced a local AI hub called the “HomeAgent,” alongside Ugreen’s new smart cameras and more. more…
fullText:
Ugreen might be most well-known for its chargers and device accessories, but its recent announcement might push it deeper into the smart home space. The company announced a local AI hub called the “HomeAgent,” alongside Ugreen’s new smart cameras and more.

With every mention of AI, there’s a little bit of unease that seems to follow. Beyond the damage it’s done to the price of anything tech these days, it also stirs privacy concerns. But a locally run AI model carries less risk, right?

Ugreen’s HomeAgent HA100 and HA100 Pro are new local AI smart home hubs that task themselves with controlling smart home devices within the ecosystem using models that run all on-device. Think of what Google Home does with AI image and event detection, but run all of it off the cloud and in a hub that sits inside your house.

The HA100 and HA100 Pro operate on your local network to handle a few tasks. The most obvious is summarized events happening around your home. Like Google Home allows with its add-on packages, the HA100 hubs can generate descriptions of what took place in front of your cameras, recognizing people, pets, and vehicles within that footage.

	

The hub will also proactively generate image highlights with the photos it has access to in its library, displaying them on Ugreen’s smart photo frames.

Ugreen says the HomeAgent hubs have Matter support. They are reportedly able to have unified local control over other devices on the network, acting as a new entry to the smart home ecosystem list.

The company also announced a set of devices that will immediately work with HomeAgent. There are three security cameras that cover indoor and outdoor needs. The Ugreen SynCare indoor camera has a pan/tilt base with 4K image capture and Wi-Fi 6 connectivity. Ugreen is clearly trying to pose its new devices as a more secure alternative, considering the indoor camera comes with a physical privacy shutter.

The SynCare PoE and Battery Cams are the two outdoor models. Both capture three video feeds with a “bullet” camera and a pan/tilt module for more coverage up to 9x hybrid zoom. The main difference between the two comes down to power delivery and placement requirements. The battery-powered option uses a solar panel to charge, but it may not be as quick to respond as the Ethernet-connected model.

snippet: Apple has hiked priced across its range of products the past few months, but the iPhone has so far escaped unscathed. fullText:
Apple has hiked priced across its range of products the past few months, but the iPhone has so far escaped unscathed. That is set to change today when Apple unveils its newest lineup of high-end iPhone models, including iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the brand new foldable device, the iPhone Duo.

But a late-breaking Bloomberg report indicates that the price increases may not be as bad as some feared. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will cost $100 more than the previous-generation, setting a new starting price of $1199.

Price increases due to rising memory component costs have been an industry-wide trend, and hit Apple starting in June, across Macs, iPads and more. But the iPhone pricing notably remained the same. 

Many assumed that the price increases for iPhone would come alongside the launch of the new 18 generation, and that is indeed happening. Gurman says the price increase will be $100.

This means Apple’s pro models will break through the previous $1099 base price, but a $100 price jump is less than what many analysts have suggested across this year. Some had predicted price jumps as high as $300.

On a related note, Gurman also says that the new foldable iPhone Duo will have a starting price of $1999, with higher-end storage capacity models reaching about $3000. This is an expensive phone, no doubt about that, but again comes in at a lower level than many predicted. 

$2199, $2299, even $2499 prices have been rumored for this device. So, just $2000 is a welcome surprise. 

Gurman writes that Apple is absorbing some of its typical margins here to hit the $2000 price point, which keeps the device competitive with the universe of Android foldables that are priced as low as $1800. Apple is expecting the iPhone Duo to be a big hit, and a marketable $1999 price will help make that happen.

Stay tuned to 9to5Mac for full coverage of everything new, when the Apple event officially kicks off later today at 10 AM PT.

title: Google’s WeatherNext 3 AI model in Search, Gemini has ’50% more accurate precipitation forecasts’
snippet: Google today announced WeatherNext 3 as its “most advanced and accurate global weather AI model,” with immediate benefits for Search and Gemini. more…
fullText:
Google today announced WeatherNext 3 as its “most advanced and accurate global weather AI model,” with immediate benefits for Search and Gemini.

Other AI weather models (including WeatherNext 2 from November 2025) are “trained on data from numerical weather prediction (NWP) models.”

Although useful, NWP models are complex, supercomputer-driven physics simulations that carry a six-hour data lag. This lag can lead to biases for fast-changing variables like rain or surface temperature.

WeatherNext 3 uses a “mosaic of live, global geostationary satellite data.” This ability to learn “directly from real-time observations” allows for a “continuously updating view of the atmosphere” that results in “timely and more localized predictions for the weather events.” The Google DeepMind and Google Research model can generate “hourly forecasts at multiple spatial resolutions.”

Temperature and moisture at 5-kilometer resolution

Surface variables at 10 kilometers

Wind speed at 25 kilometers

A forecast’s utility often comes down to detail and how finely it resolves both time and space.

Compared to WeatherNext 2’s 25-kilometer grid in 6-hour increments, this update provides a global weather picture that is “roughly five times sharper.”

	

This is important because critical weather develops fast. When storms, fronts, or precipitation systems materialize suddenly, our rapid update cycle and higher resolution provides earlier, more detailed insights needed to help drive an effective response.

Google also touts a “significant leap in precipitation forecasting accuracy” by training WeatherNext 3 with “two exceptionally high-quality sources of precipitation data: NASA’s satellite-based Integrated Multi-satellite Retrievals for GPM (IMERG) and our own global precipitation reanalysis based on satellite radar.”

In medium-range global forecasts, evaluations against baselines show a Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) improvement of up to 60% against IMERG, 30% for MRMS, and 10% against rain gauge measurements for early lead times.

Other benefits include:

“This breakthrough is particularly vital for regions across Latin America, Africa, and Asia-Pacific that have historically been underserved by high-resolution forecasting due to the immense supercomputing costs of traditional regional models. It brings localized, high-fidelity forecasting to billions of people and local businesses in these areas.”

“Beyond improved resolution and forecast frequency, our model introduces predictions specifically engineered for renewable energy production. The model forecasts 100-meter wind speeds (roughly at turbine-height) for precise wind-energy output, alongside high-resolution cloud cover and sun radiation levels to help solar farms estimate how much light they will receive on the ground.”

In terms of consumer-facing benefits, WeatherNext 3 is rolling out to Google Search, Maps, and the Gemini app. Google says to expect “dramatically improve[d] longer term forecasts.”

When planning a day or more ahead, people will see up to 50% more accurate precipitation forecasts — with the greatest improvements in regions where forecasts have historically been less reliable.
