title: Apple unveils its first foldable, the iPhone Duo
snippet: Unlike early iterations of foldables, which looked like vertical slabs, Apple adopted a wider form factor that could aid in a better aspect ratio while watching videos when the device is unfolded.
fullText:
Apple today introduced its first foldable device, named the iPhone Duo, at its Surprise and Shine event held in Cupertino. The phone is the first marquee device launched under the company’s new CEO, John Ternus.

Unlike early iterations of foldables, which looked like vertical slabs, Apple adopted a wider form factor that could aid in a better aspect ratio while watching videos when the device is unfolded.

Image Credits:Apple

The unfolded display is a 7.6-inch Retina display, and the outer display is 5.4 inches. The company said that the new device was “inspired by the versatility of iPad” and showed how people can use it unfolded in a vertical mode. The inner display also features an “under-display” camera that can give users an all-screen feel.

Apple said that it used a custom nanotexture finish to hide the crease and reduce glare. Most foldables still have a visible crease, but companies like Oppo have made strides toward an almost seamless phone. The company claimed that its hinge was created using grade 5 aluminum and over 100 special components for smooth opening and closing and durability.

Notably, the device only has Touch ID, with Face ID missing. You can unlock the device using the Apple Watch, though. 

The device is powered by the new A20 Pro chip and C2 model, which allows for faster uploads. Just like last year’s iPhone Air, this particular model is eSIM-only.

On the battery front, the company said that with the inner display, users can get 31 hours of video playback, and with the outer display, 44 hours of video playback.

The phone features a 48-megapixel fusion main camera and a 48-megapixel ultrawide camera with 2x optical zoom. This dual-camera setup skips a telephoto camera. Just like other foldables, users can take rear-camera selfies and look at previews on the outer display. It also has a Google Pixel-like feature that plays an animation on the outer display, which is useful when you are trying to get kids to focus while taking photos. There is also a smart-take feature that uses an on-device model and snaps an image when all subjects within the frame are posing.

The company has made iOS 27 adaptable to the new foldable — essential controls like Wi-Fi move to the side and dock on the home screen vertically oriented. Users can use apps in split screen and also pair the apps. If someone is using the phone vertically, they can pin a video on top and use other apps in the bottom half. One of the fascinating features is that users will be able to use the iPhone half folded or even set it on a table. Apple noted that later this year, the device will support Apple Pencil.

The iPhone Duo is priced at $1,999 with 256GB storage and comes in two colors. Preorders for Apple’s new foldable begin on October 16, and the device will be available on October 23.

Rivals like Samsung and Xiaomi have already launched their version of wide foldables before Apple.

According to analytics firm Counterpoint, foldables contribute to less than 2% of shipments in the overall smartphone market. However, Apple’s new phone could be an instant hit, as the analytics firm said the Duo could garner up to 25% market share by the end of the year.

title: Hands-on: Nothing’s $25 CMF Buds Neo are way better than the price suggests
snippet: Last month, Nothing’s CMF brand launched a new pair of $25 earbuds in the CMF Buds Neo. Too good to be true, I figured, but after getting my hands on them, I’m pleasantly surprised by what they bring to the table despite some expected downsides. more…
fullText:
Last month, Nothing’s CMF brand launched a new pair of $25 earbuds in the CMF Buds Neo. Too good to be true, I figured, but after getting my hands on them, I’m pleasantly surprised by what they bring to the table despite some expected downsides.

The CMF Buds Neo bring a lot to the table on paper. 52-hour battery life, active noise cancellation, some flashy colors, and even dual-device connections alongside support for the Nothing X app and EQ presets. For $25, it’s a compelling package. 

How does it deliver in real life?

I’ve spent a few hours listening to CMF Buds Neo and, honestly, I’m pretty impressed!

	

At their core, they get the job done. The earbuds have decent sound quality, though they’re a bit hollow on default settings. I found that turning down the bass enhancement improves the sound quality, and they’re more optimized for speech (podcasts, etc) than music. Nothing Ear (3a) sound far better; don’t get me wrong, but probably not 4x better as the price on paper suggests.

The sound quality is the most important thing here when the price is so low, and it’s certainly more than good enough to make these a good deal. And there’s clearly more weight put in the price than anything else. CMF Buds Neo have some clear and obvious downsides. The case is cheap-feeling despite looking very nice, and the same goes for the earbuds – the materials feel cheap, but they fit nice in my ear and stay comfortable over a few hours of use. The touchpads on the earbuds are responsive, but lack a play/pause gesture by default. Another downside is the range, as I found these disconnect from my Fold 8 more quickly than other earbuds I’ve tested in recent memory. The case magnets that hold the earbuds in place work well, and there are some nice touches such as a snappy hinge and the lanyard hole on a rotating corner piece. 

There’s also no pairing button on the case, something that will never fail to annoy me, but at least there’s Google Fast Pair – humorously, the Fast Pair pop-up lacks a picture of the earbuds and just says “blue” on the variant I bought.

Downsides are aplenty here, which really shouldn’t come as a surprise. But, at the core, you’re getting earbuds that sound good enough, have most important features, and cost just $25. If you need a spare pair of earbuds to throw in a backpack or at your bedside, or a daily driver on a budget, these are a winner in my book.

title: Apple shows off AirPods 5 with improved active noise cancellation
snippet: The AirPods 5 support better noise cancellation, Siri AI, and offer volume controls on the stem.
fullText:
At Apple’s Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday, the company unveiled the latest generation of its wireless earbuds, the AirPods 5, introducing several upgrades like improved audio, stronger active noise cancellation, and expanded Siri and Apple Intelligence features.

One of the main upgrades is active noise cancellation. Apple says AirPods 5 can reduce background noise by 50% more than the previous generation, making them “the industry’s best” active noise cancellation, according to the company.

“We’re thrilled that with AirPods 5, active noise cancelation is now standard across our entire AirPods lineup. AirPods 5 are a great example of how we take the innovations from our most advanced products and bring them to the rest of the lineup, making them accessible to even more people,” CEO John Ternus said during the event.

Image Credits:Apple

Apple has also added volume control to the stem, a feature previously available only with the AirPods Pro. Users can swipe up or down on the stem to change the volume without reaching for their iPhone.

As with other models with the H2 chip, AirPods 5 also offer hands-free Siri and Apple Intelligence features. Users can interact with Siri without picking up their phone, whether they want to ask a question, find information, perform an action, or get directions.

The updated Siri, which Apple says will roll out in beta with iOS 27, is designed to better understand personal context. It can use information from messages, emails, photos, and other apps to provide more relevant responses and complete tasks. For example, Siri could find a restaurant mentioned in an email or play a song a friend recommended in a message.

Transparency mode in AirPods 5 has also been improved, allowing users to hear nearby voices and sounds more naturally. Adaptive Audio can automatically balance noise cancellation and Transparency mode, depending on the surrounding environment. Conversation Awareness, meanwhile, can lower the media volume when the user begins speaking.

Additionally, battery life received an upgrade, with AirPods 5 offering up to five hours of listening with active noise cancellation on a single charge. The charging case brings total listening time up to 22 hours with active noise cancellation enabled. 

AirPods 5 start at $129, while the version with a Wireless Charging Case costs $149. Preorders begin today, with the earbuds arriving September 18.

title: Not Every Feature Apple Announced Is Ready to Go. Here’s When to Expect Them All
snippet: Some of the most interesting features won’t ship with the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.
fullText:
The first question following an Apple event — after “Can I really afford that?” — is always “When can I get it?” And consistent with previous product announcements, some of the devices and features that Apple revealed Wednesday won’t be available for a while.

Fortunately, it doesn’t seem like we’re seeing a repeat of 2024’s Apple Intelligence rollout, which inspired a false-claims lawsuit, which Apple is settling. Siri AI now works as advertised, at least in the beta versions we’ve tested so far.

For the other features Apple touted during its event, here’s an idea of when you’ll actually be able to get them in your hands. We have specific dates for a few things, but be prepared to wait until “late 2026” for several. 

The main events: Hardware

Some of Apple’s new products are just around the corner, while others require a wait.

The Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and AirPods 5 can be preordered now and will arrive starting Sept. 18.

Preorders for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max open at 5 a.m. PT on Saturday and will also begin arriving on Sept. 18.

The star of the show, the foldable iPhone Duo, is a bit further out, with preorders starting at 5 a.m. PT on Oct. 16 and first shipments arriving Oct. 23.

It will be a month before you, too, can get an iPhone Duo in your hands.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

The system updates

The new hardware will include the latest versions of the operating systems, such as iOS 27 for iPhone models, but if you own an existing device, you’ll be able to run the software earlier. iOS 27, iPadOS 27, WatchOS 27, MacOS 27 Golden Gate, TVOS 27 and VisionOS 27 will all be available to install on Sept. 14.

Apple Intelligence features coming soon

Siri AI is still officially a beta feature, and Apple says it will “roll out gradually” in English after the launch of the new operating systems. Siri AI will be available in October in French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish. In the developer and public betas, you had to request access to the feature and wait for it to be activated, so I expect that will be the case at release, too.

On the new Apple Watch models, Live Rewind and Siri Recap are listed as available in beta in late 2026 and will require the watch to be paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone 16 or later (except for the iPhone 16e).

The Suggestions in the Messages app, where a button appears within a conversation to take contextual action – such as adding an item to your calendar – is also “coming in a future software update,” although I’ve seen it in the iOS 27 public betas.

Screenshot by CNET/Apple

Miscellaneous features

Several features that don’t fit neatly into the above categories are also arriving sometime after the new devices and system software ship.

The Passwords app can fix weak or compromised passwords by logging into a site in the background and updating the password on its own. This will be included in a future software update.

iPhone Handoff, the feature that lets you share a phone number between two iPhones, will initially be available to T-Mobile subscribers in the US and to Telecom Germany subscribers. Verizon and EE will get support by the end of the year.

Monster Hunter Outlanders, which was shown to demonstrate the gaming abilities of the iPhone models, is coming later this year.

The iPhone Duo is getting support for the Apple Pencil – but not the Apple Pencil Pro – on both iPhone Duo displays, and it’s arriving later this year.

Health features

The Health app on iPhone is getting a redesign that will be coming in late 2026. That will also add the Health Age feature that looks at seven sources of data, such as sleep and activity, to gauge your current health level.

The redesign will also include personalized guidance recommendations, such as adding intervals to a run to increase your cardio.

title: Gemini app makes Daily Brief free in the US
snippet: After introducing at I/O 2026 in May, Google is making Daily Brief in the Gemini app available for free in the US. more…
fullText:
After introducing at I/O 2026 in May, Google is making Daily Brief in the Gemini app available for free in the US.

Daily Brief generates a list of your to-dos and priorities every morning. Gemini uses Personal Intelligence to look at your Gmail, Google Calendar, and other Connected Apps, as well as past Gemini chats.

The Daily Brief starts with a “Top of mind” section that shows “timely, actionable items,” such as tasks with upcoming deadlines. “FYI” will show other items that have dates attached. “Looking ahead” is the final section with a focus on long-term goals and “suggested next steps to help you achieve them.”

You can tap on items to “Mark complete” or start a “Chat” with Gemini. There’s also the ability to leave “Helpful” or “Not helpful” feedback.

	

Example use cases include:

For students: Manage class schedules, organize study plans, and track applications.

For entrepreneurs: Surface actionable client emails and update task reminders.

For parents: Manage school communications, track family milestones, and handle household tasks.

For job seekers: Quickly act on recruiter inquiries, prepare for interviews, and monitor application statuses.

As of last Friday, Gemini Daily Brief no longer requires a Google AI subscription in the US. It’s available to personal Google Accounts with Personal Intelligence, Memory, and the Google Workspace integration enabled.

You can access it from the Gemini side panel, with Google also sending a notification every morning. You can disable that alert by going to the account menu and configuring “Notifications.” 

Another way to interact with the digest is through Gemini Live: “What’s my daily brief?”

title: iPhone 18 Pro set to become Apple’s new default model
snippet: iPhone 18 Pro is about to be unveiled, and due to a lineup overhaul this year, it’s set to become Apple’s new default model like never before. more…
fullText:
iPhone 18 Pro is about to be unveiled, and due to a lineup overhaul this year, it’s set to become Apple’s new default model like never before.

With no base iPhone 18 available, iPhone 18 Pro will be Apple’s default new model this year

Apple has offered multiple new iPhone models every year for a very long time. And no doubt will for many years to come.

But at this week’s Apple event, a big shakeup is coming to the iPhone lineup.

Rather than launching the typical ‘iPhone’ and ‘iPhone Pro’ options, the base model iPhone 18 will be missing.

Numerous reports point to Apple pushing back the release of iPhone 18 and also iPhone Air 2 into early 2027. That leaves a fall lineup consisting only of:

iPhone 18 Pro

iPhone 18 Pro Max

iPhone Ultra

By delaying iPhone 18 beyond its typical release schedule, iPhone 18 Pro will essentially become Apple’s new default model.

Users who need a cheaper device will still be able to choose from last year’s iPhone 17, or the iPhone 17e or iPhone Air. But in all the marketing we see from Apple and carrier partners this fall and into the holidays, there will be no ‘iPhone 18’ to promote as the new default. Instead, iPhone 18 Pro will fill that role.

iPhone Ultra will be too expensive, and likely fairly niche in comparison.

So for the average person who wants “the new iPhone,” Apple will basically have just two options: iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max.

It’s an interesting experiment, and could see iPhone 18 Pro become the new bestselling Pro model. But paired with expected price increases, it’s also a risk for Apple. Prospective upgraders might hold on to their current iPhone longer because there’s no iPhone 18 to upgrade to.

One way or another, we’ll find out very soon whether Apple’s new plan pays off.

title: Xbox Game Pass will get a Google TV app ‘in the coming months,’ likely only for TCL
snippet: Following a prior teaser that was the better part of a year ago, Microsoft has finally acknowledged its work on a Google TV app for Xbox Game Pass on TCL TVs, but it’s still “months” out from the sound of it. more…
fullText:
Following a prior teaser that was the better part of a year ago, Microsoft has finally acknowledged its work on a Google TV app for Xbox Game Pass on TCL TVs, but it’s still “months” out from the sound of it.

TCL first announced that an Xbox Game Pass app would be coming to its TVs – the Google TV models, specifically – back at CES 2026. That was in January. Microsoft never acknowledged the announcement publicly, and it’s been months since we’ve gotten any updates.

Today, Microsoft has officially confirmed that it will release an Xbox Game Pass app on TCL TVs, marking the first time the cloud gaming service will officially be available on Google TV. Microsoft’s announcement never formally acknowledges Google TV by name, hinting that this is probably exclusive to TCL TVs, rather than being available for the broader platform. TCL is the biggest Google TV partner and, while it also produces Roku and Fire TV units, it primarily uses Google TV and had previously teased the Xbox app directly around its new Google TV flagship.

But the Xbox Game Pass app for TCL’s Google TV sets is apparently still “months” away, despite the nine-month gap we’ve already gone through since the collaboration was first announced.

	

Microsoft says:

Today, we’re sharing a new partnership with TCL that will bring the XBOX app to select TCL Smart TVs in the coming months…

…With the XBOX app on supported TCL Smart TVs, players will be able to access XBOX Cloud Gaming through their Game Pass subscription to stream supported games directly from their TV. For eligible XBOX Game Pass subscribers, that means access to an instant library of games spanning blockbuster releases, beloved franchises, and indie favorites through their cloud playtime.

This comes just a day after Microsoft announced major changes to its cloud gaming setup on Xbox Game Pass. Players will now have a limited number of hours per month, topping out at 15 hours, before they need to pay more.

title: Apple releases iPadOS 27 RC, plus watchOS 27 and more
snippet: Today following its “Surprise and shine” September event, Apple has shipped the RC (release candidate) versions of iPadOS 27, watchOS 27, and more. more…
fullText:
Today following its “Surprise and shine” September event, Apple has shipped the RC (release candidate) versions of iPadOS 27, watchOS 27, and more.

RC versions of iPadOS 27 and more available now for testing

Apple’s major new software updates for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and more are almost here.

iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS Golden Gate, watchOS 27, tvOS 27, and visionOS 27 will ship to all users next week on Monday, September 14.

After a full summer of beta testing, today Apple is rolling out the RC versions of those updates.

Developers and public beta testers can install the RC for iPadOS 27 and more via the Software Update screen in Settings.

Release candidate builds are intended to be the final shipping software that launches to all users. But if Apple discovers any critical issues that need to be patched, we may see RC 2 builds debut soon.

It’s become common practice for Apple to ship the RC builds of its major new software updates right after the annual iPhone launch event. 

That’s because there are often new features not announced at WWDC that remain hidden until the September event. For example, today Apple detailed watchOS 27 changes during the Apple Watch hardware unveiling that were not mentioned in June—but are now available in the watchOS 27 RC.

title: Lenovo’s first RTX Spark laptops can have up to 128GB of RAM
snippet: IFA 2026 is underway with Lenovo’s Innovation World event seeing the debut of the company’s first RTX Spark laptops as well as a flagship Android tablet and more. more…
fullText:
IFA 2026 is underway with Lenovo’s Innovation World event seeing the debut of the company’s first RTX Spark laptops as well as a flagship Android tablet and more.

Starting off with laptops, Lenovo is using Nvidia’s new RTX Spark chip in new Yoga machines – and they sound nuts.

The Lenovo Yoga Pro 9n is a 15-inch with a 2560×1600 OLED display, up to 128GB of RAM, two SSD slots and up to 4TB of storage, and a 92.5Whr battery with 140W charging and a “Rapid Charge Express” mode that buys 3 hours of battery life in 15 minutes. For ports, it has two USB-C (40GBps) and two USB-A ports on either side, as well as HDMI and a full-size SD card slot. That’s all in a machine that’s “as thin as” 16.7mm and weighs 3.64lbs. It also has a haptic trackpad which has pen support.

Again, it sounds nuts.

	

The other option is the Yoga 9n 2-in-1 with a 16-inch display. It has a 2880×1800 OLED display, the same Nvidia RTX Spark chip, but is a bit tamer throughout the rest of the package. Up to 64GB of RAM, up to 2TB of SSD storage, but the same ports. Battery life is powered by a 99.9Whr battery with the same fast-charging setup, but this one is thicker at 17.5mm and weighs in at 4.28lbs.

Lenovo is directly positioning these machines at professional creators, with a focus on raw power for video editing, 3D rendering, and local AI applications. 

As you might imagine in the midst of RAMageddon, Lenovo isn’t confirming prices for either of these machines just yet, and there’s no release window either.

title: Google Search kicks off the NFL season with Live Game Feeds and fantasy football advice
snippet: Tonight’s game between the New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks isn’t just a Super Bowl LX rematch — it’s also the official start of the 2026 NFL season. Google has invested pretty heavily in football over the past few years through YouTube TV, but today, it’s giving Search some big improvements to make following the season a little easier. more…
fullText:
Tonight’s game between the New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks isn’t just a Super Bowl LX rematch — it’s also the official start of the 2026 NFL season. Google has invested pretty heavily in football over the past few years through YouTube TV, but today, it’s giving Search some big improvements to make following the season a little easier.

Google is adding a Live Game Feed to search, which allows fans and spectators alike to follow along with game developments as they unfold on the field. Any active game will show a “Live” icon in search, and selecting that option shows a recap of what’s happened so far alongside a “dynamic timeline featuring play-by-play updates, top social commentary, key video highlights, and AI-powered insights.” This sounds quite a bit like Google’s alternative to something like Apple’s (truly excellent) sports app, though we’ll have to see how it performs in action first.

Meanwhile, Search is also getting a new carousel display that shows other ongoing games whenever you search for a specific matchup, alongside a stats page that shows player-specific performance like rushing yards, sacks, and YAC, with favorability metrics on their way. Finally, Google has tuned AI Mode to assist with your fantasy football lineup, supporting Yahoo Fantasy and Sleeper account sync directly for real-time suggestions ahead of kickoff on Sunday.

Google’s new carousel view in Search is rolling out to all users globally on mobile. Live Game Feed is available in the US in English and currently supports NFL games, with a broader expansion and plans to add collegiate teams coming later this month. Fantasy football advice in AI Mode is, similarly, only available for English-language users in the US.

More on Google:

Google is making AI Overviews even bigger on some search queries

title: Three new iPhones launch this week, here’s what’s coming
snippet: Apple’s big September event is this Wednesday, and the company has three new iPhone models set to launch: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo. Here’s what to expect. more…
fullText:
Apple’s big September event is this Wednesday, and the company has three new iPhone models set to launch: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo. Here’s what to expect.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max

iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are coming as successors to Apple’s popular 17 Pro line.

New features that are rumored include:

A20 Pro chip for more power and efficiency

Major camera upgrades, especially to the Main camera with variable aperture

35% smaller Dynamic Island for more modern design

New colors, headlined by a bold burgundy

Best battery life ever, with iPhone 18 Pro Max getting big gains

Camera Control gets a revamp

C2 cellular modem designed by Apple

New satellite features, including 5G

iPhone 18 Pro is also expected to have a higher starting price. Estimates suggest it could start at $1,399, but I suspect it could be closer to $1,199 or $1,249.

iPhone Duo

‘iPhone Ultra’ has long been the rumored name for Apple’s first foldable, but the latest leaks say it will be called iPhone Duo instead. We’re expecting a $2,000+ price, creating a new high-end tier.

The foldable form factor should make iPhone Duo the most radically unique model Apple has yet introduced. It will have a wide book-style fold, with a roughly 5.4-inch outer display and 7.8-inch inner display that resembles an iPad mini.

Design materials are expected to mimic the iPhone Air, with a titanium border and sleek look.

iPhone Duo will have two rear cameras (Main and Ultra Wide) plus two front-facing cameras, one for each display. It will use Touch ID for authentication rather than Face ID.

Software will be where the device especially shines, with iOS 27 supporting side-by-side app multitasking and adaptive landscape layouts that are perfect for the new form factor.

Performance should be about the same as iPhone 18 Pro, with the same A20 Pro chip, a vapor chamber for cooling, and a C2 modem.

What’s missing: iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2

Normally we would expect a new base model iPhone 18 to launch in September too, alongside an iPhone Air successor.

This year though, Apple is reportedly overhauling its fall lineup by pushing the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 into early 2027.

It’s unknown whether this change is entirely strategic, or simply out of necessity due to the current memory crisis. In any case, the absence of more affordable models means this fall’s new iPhone line will focus solely on the high end.

title: Google Maps speedometer disappears on Android Auto for some, traffic data still missing too
snippet: Android Auto users are reporting an issue where the Google Maps speedometer, available for mere months, is randomly vanishing. more…
fullText:
Android Auto users are reporting an issue where the Google Maps speedometer, available for mere months, is randomly vanishing.

Back in July, Google Maps on Android Auto finally started rolling out support for a live speedometer while navigating. This was alongside showing speed limits. It started more broadly rolling out later that month, but still hasn’t rolled out to everyone.

Now, in fact, we’re looking at the exact opposite happening. A number of users have reported on Reddit that the speedometer has suddenly vanished on Android Auto. It’s not a particularly widespread issue, it seems, but the rollout hasn’t expanded to all users in the first place. This is alongside traffic patterns, which are still missing for a number of users after breaking in late August. 

We’ve also noticed continued reports of Android Auto missing its signal indicator, an ongoing bug for months at this point.

	

Google rolls out new Android Auto updates on a pretty regular basis, along with Maps, but these isolated issues just don’t seem to be going away. Leave a comment below if you’re running into these problems.

title: OpenAI releases ChatGPT Images 2.5 with ‘sharper details’ and ‘more precise editing’
snippet: In April, OpenAI released upgraded image generation technology with ChatGPT Images 2. Five months later, the company is releasing an enhanced version, ChatGPT Images 2.5. more…
fullText:
In April, OpenAI released upgraded image generation technology with ChatGPT Images 2. Five months later, the company is releasing an enhanced version, ChatGPT Images 2.5. 

ChatGPT Images 2 was a notable leap over the company’s earlier image generation tools.

It added 2K resolution output, multiple aspect ratio support, and the ability to use web research for up-to-date information. Images 2 also added non-Latin language expertise and two intelligence levels: Instant and Thinking.

The latest Images 2.5 version touts “sharper details, faster generation, more precise editing, and better tools for creating and sharing.”

“Images 2.5 produces more natural lighting and richer textures, is better at preserving the subjects in your reference photos, and follows editing instructions more reliably across multiple turns,” OpenAI says.

“We’ve also reduced image generation latency by up to 50% compared with Images 2.0, so you can generate images and refine your concepts more quickly.”

Additionally, the company details a new “Sketch” feature that enables drawing directly in ChatGPT. This can be used as a reference for image generation. Plus OpenAI is introducing templates for popular image formats, prompt sharing for others to try your ideas related to image-gen, and more.

Additionally, OpenAI is releasing two versions of Images 2.5 for developers to build around in their apps. GPT-Image-2.5 Flare and GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburt will be available through OpenAI’s API:

GPT‑Image‑2.5 Flare brings the same improvements in quality, editing, and speed to the API and is the default choice for most applications, delivering higher-quality images than GPT‑Image‑2 at 50% lower latency. It’s well suited to everything from creator and social content to product experiences, visual search, rapid image prototyping, and high-volume generation.

GPT‑Image‑2.5 Sunburst is built for premium visual workflows that benefit from tighter control across edits. Use it for creative and editing workflows like production-ready campaign creative or polished product imagery.

“Images 2.5 is rolling out today to ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex users across all tiers on desktop, mobile, and web,” according to OpenAI. You can learn more about the new image-gen technology here.

Today’s ChatGPT Images 2.5 release follows last week’s GPT-6 Astra launch.

title: macOS 27 Golden Gate: Here are Apple’s full release notes
snippet: Apple has announced that macOS 27 Golden Gate will ship to all users next Monday, September 14. Here are Apple’s official release notes for macOS 27. more…
fullText:
Apple has announced that macOS 27 Golden Gate will ship to all users next Monday, September 14. Here are Apple’s official release notes for macOS 27.

Apple’s official macOS 27 release notes now available

Today alongside shipping its RC (release candidate) updates, Apple published full release notes for iOS 27 and also for macOS 27 Golden Gate.

Here are the full, unedited macOS 27 release notes:

Experience the new Siri AI

Introducing Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence that’s more personal, more capable, and more conversational. It is integrated into Spotlight, so you can search for answers about almost any topic right from where you already search for things across your system. It can draw on personal context to find things across your messages, mail, photos, and more. And it can get things done across your apps, just by asking. Revisit and resume past conversations in the new dedicated Siri app, synced with iCloud across your Apple devices. Siri AI is rolling out to users, and you can get started by turning it on in Settings.

Take action on what’s onscreen

With Visual Intelligence, you can select a window of your screen and Siri can answer questions or take action with what’s onscreen, like adding events to your calendar. You can access Visual Intelligence with a dedicated keyboard shortcut — Command-Shift-Space.

Powerful new ways to edit photos

Use intelligent photo editing tools to reframe a photo after it’s been taken with Spatial Reframing or expand your shot with the Extend tool. And enhancements to Clean Up let you remove distractions with better quality and more realistic infill, even when the scene is complex.

New tools to browse in Safari

Automatically group your tabs into topics, so related pages are easier to find. With Notify Me, Safari can monitor pages for changes like price drops or restocks and alert you when it’s time to act. Describe an Extension lets you use natural language to create custom extensions, like adding a button to save your favorite recipes.

Easily create Shortcuts using natural language

With Describe a Shortcut, you can automate daily tasks with a simple description and all of the required steps are assembled on your behalf. For example, you can describe a shortcut to automatically text your partner when you’re headed home from work with an estimated arrival time based on traffic.

Even more refined design

Updates to Liquid Glass improve readability, and a new slider lets you customize how it looks, from ultra-clear to fully tinted. Uniform toolbars, edge-to-edge sidebars, and more detailed app icons further elevate the design.

New child safety features

Powerful new parental controls help parents more easily manage what content their children can see, who they can communicate with, and when they have access to apps. Ask to Browse requires kids to request permission before visiting any new website in Safari. Communication Safety expands its protections to help keep conversations safe. Time Allowances gives parents more flexible ways to manage the time kids spend in apps across categories, and offers guidance based on expert research that’s tailored to a child’s age. Schedules help manage which apps kids have access to at different times of the day and across the week.

A more responsive and delightful experience

An expansive set of improvements make your Mac even faster, more reliable, and easier to use. Better search in Spotlight and Mail helps you find what you’re looking for with greater ease. AirDrop Transfers and network file browsing happen faster. And many more improvements make your day-to-day use more enjoyable.

For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: support.apple.com/100100.

Some features may not be available in all regions or on all Apple devices. To learn more, please visit: apple.com/macos/feature-availability.

Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features, including but not limited to Siri AI, Intelligent Photo Editing Tools, Image Playground and AFM 3 Cloud models in Shortcuts. To learn more please visit: apple.com/apple-intelligence.

title: I Got My Hands on the iPhone Duo, Apple’s First Foldable Phone. Here’s What Stands Out
snippet: The palm-size phone is Apple’s boldest handset in years, with a 5.4-inch cover screen and a 7.6-inch main display. I spent some time with the Duo before its October launch.
fullText:
It’s finally here: Apple on Wednesday unveiled its first foldable iPhone, called the iPhone Duo. It’ll start at $1,999 for 256GB in the US. Preorders for the iPhone Duo begin on Oct. 16, ahead of an Oct. 23 release.

Apple debuted the new device during its fall event in Cupertino, California, along with the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. It appears the company will save the baseline iPhone 18 for a later reveal, likely in spring 2027. 

Similar to Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8, the iPhone Duo is designed to be better suited for consuming all kinds of media. If you’re watching a YouTube video or movie, the inside display gives you plenty of room. Rotate it to portrait, and you can endlessly scroll through vertical videos or read an e-book. The compact cover screen can be handy for quickly sending a message or checking notifications. It’s essentially designed to function as a compact iPhone that can double as an iPad Mini when needed.

I spent some time with the iPhone Duo at Apple Park, and here are a few features that stand out to me.

iPhone Duo design and build

The iPhone Duo is compact, with a passport-size design. It has a 7.6-inch display on the inside and a 5.4-inch outer display. It fits squarely in my palm, with dimensions similar to Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8, which has a 7.6-inch inner display and a 5.5-inch cover display.

Apple says the Duo is the thinnest iPhone ever when open, measuring 5.2mm. It’s 11.3mm thick when closed. A titanium frame keeps it lightweight at 254 grams. 

One of the key differences in feel between Apple’s and Samsung’s phones is that the iPhone Duo has a matte, nano-textured finish on the inner display, which reduces the phone’s crease while also curbing reflections. It has a satisfying feel and really makes the crease virtually disappear when the screen is on. I find it even harder to notice than the Z Fold 8’s, which also has an anti-reflective display.

What crease??Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

While the Z Fold 8 has sharper corners, the iPhone Duo takes on more rounded edges. Which look you prefer comes down to preference. For now, I’m partial to the Z Fold 8’s more square-like design that makes it appear slightly more polished , but it’s possible the Duo’s style will grow on me.

There’s another distinguishing trait on the iPhone Duo. When opening the phone, the content transitions from the cover screen to the main display almost immediately. On the other hand, when I prop the Z Fold 8 open, content shifts from the cover to the main display when it’s about halfway open. It’s a neat element that can help the Duo feel more refined; I’m just not sure if it’ll make a significant difference in the user experience. I’ll need more time with the phone to decide.  

The Duo supports multitasking with up to two apps. The Z Fold 8, in comparison, supports up to three apps (though things get a little crowded, so I tend to stick to two).

Interestingly, the Duo’s volume buttons are at the top of the phone when holding it in landscape. That prevents them from being cluttered amid the lock and Camera Control buttons, but it might take some time to get used to the placement. On the other hand, it’ll be easier to adjust the volume when the phone is rotated to portrait.

The Duo’s volume controls sit at the top of the phone.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

The Duo’s cover is made with Apple’s Ceramic Shield 2, while Ceramic Shield protects the back. Perhaps one of the Duo’s most impressive traits is the IP68 rating for dust and water resistance, putting it on par with the durable Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold. Apple says a titanium plate helps to improve the Duo’s durability. 

The iPhone Duo’s hinge is made of more than 100 components, according to Apple, making for a smooth open and close. The unfolding mechanism did give off a silky, premium feel as I repeatedly unfurled and shut the display. 

The iPhone Duo can be propped half-open to easily watch movies and access controls.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

Apple’s foldable comes in two colors, dubbed star white and night sky, which is a navy hue. It’ll be compatible with the Apple Pencil, which separates it from the Z Fold 8, which sadly doesn’t support Samsung’s S Pen. 

To unlock, the Duo supports Touch ID, rather than Face ID. That’s a bit of a letdown, especially at such a high price. But I tend to use fingerprint unlock on the Z Fold 8 anyway, so perhaps it won’t be much of an adjustment for everyone.

Like the iPhone 18 Pro models, the Duo is powered by the A20 Pro chip.

iPhone Duo cameras

There are only two rear cameras.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

The iPhone Duo has a 48-megapixel main camera and a 48-megapixel ultrawide camera. Like the Z Fold 8, there’s no telephoto camera. I didn’t mind the lack of a telephoto lens on Samsung’s foldable, so I’m curious if I’ll feel the same once I take Apple’s new foldable out into the world to snap some photos. 

The iPhone Duo supports 4K video at 120 frames per second in Dolby Vision, as well as 4K time-lapse video in Dolby Vision HDR. 

Dual Capture in FaceTime lets you use the front and rear cameras simultaneously. When taking photos, you can turn on Duo Preview on the cover screen when the phone is unfolded, so your subject can see how the shot will look as you snap with the rear cameras. A feature called Kid Cue displays Peanuts animations on the cover screen to help draw kids’ eyes to the camera. This is similar to Made You Look on Pixel’s foldables. 

Duo Preview in action.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

iPhone Duo battery life

Apple says the iPhone Duo will give you up to 31 hours of video playback on the inner display, and 44 hours when using the outer screen. When using both equally, the company says you’ll be able to go 24 hours before needing to charge.

Considering how often I use both the cover and inside displays on the Galaxy Z Fold 8, I have a feeling my battery life would lean more toward that 24-hour mark. But we’ll have to see how the phone holds up in CNET’s battery tests.

Apple/Screenshot by CNET

A new foldable competitor 

With the iPhone Duo, Apple enters an increasingly competitive foldable phone market, with key players including Samsung, Google and Motorola, as well as Chinese brands like Honor, Oppo and Huawei. Now, it’s Apple’s turn to further shape the space – and likely nudge it forward.

Analysts predict the iPhone Duo could give foldables, which remain a niche smartphone category, a significant boost. IDC forecasts that global foldable shipments will grow by more than 12% this year, with Apple’s entry driving much of that growth. The research firm also expects Apple to ship more than 17 million foldable iPhones by 2027, giving the company nearly 40% global market share by the end of next year.

“The iPhone Duo is the event’s strategic flagship and a direct test of whether Apple can use design, ecosystem integration and premium positioning to reshape a segment that has so far remained selective,” said Francisco Jeronimo, vice president of devices at IDC.

In addition to her current role, she's worked for CNET's video, culture and news teams. title: US Army places $11M bet on Austin-based GPS alternative Tern
snippet: Tern has described its tech as "Google Maps for the battlefield."
fullText:
Austin-based Tern has won a contract from the U.S. Army to deploy the startup’s low-cost GPS alternative tech. 

The $11.26 million contract will see the Army use Tern’s navigation tech in vehicles, though the startup was tight-lipped on the exact scale of the deployment of what it calls “Google Maps for the battlefield.” 

The Army is tapping Tern at a time when GPS disruptions are on the rise, especially in the Middle East and in the skies above Ukraine and Russia. The U.S. military itself has reportedly been experimenting with GPS jamming, which may have even contributed to the deadly crash of a medevac plane earlier this year. There have been multiple efforts from Congress and President Trump (during his first term) to develop resilient, non-GPS navigation technologies for military use. 

Modern vehicles generate all kinds of data while driving, and Tern’s whole tech stack is oriented around using some of that information to navigate without GPS. 

“We’ve got a device that plugs into the diagnostics board of the vehicle, wired to a tablet, and then that tablet is the interface for the soldier to use, and we provide both the position and navigation and routing there for the soldier,” Tern co-founder and CEO Shaun Moore said in an interview. 

Moore said Tern is “passively listening to” this information and not disrupting its flow in any way. Tern then uses “proprietary methods” to make the information usable for navigation. (He declined to go into specifics.) 

“There is quite a bit of work that was done to get it to the point where we can just receive that information and then output latitude / longitude, so big effort by our team,” he said. 

All this allows a vehicle to essentially determine its own position independently, using edge processing, which is helpful both on- and off-road, in tunnels or in deserts. Moore’s co-founder Brett Harrison even recently used it to navigate a 1,300-mile drive between Austin and Laguna Beach, California. He said Tern’s tech never lost his vehicle’s place during the whole trip, while traditional GPS cut out dozens of times.

Another aspect of Tern’s tech that may be just as important as accurate positioning is that it’s a closed system. This means it is not just a backup, it’s actually harder for adversaries to disrupt it.

“I don’t know that there is broad awareness on the fragility of the [GPS] system from a consumer standpoint,” Moore said. “I think people just see the blue dot on their phone and say it will always be there because it’s there now, right? Why wouldn’t it be there?”

As a military vet himself, Harrison said the Army contract is validating after Tern spent years proving that its tech works. He said his time in Afghanistan as part of a special operations task force is a big part of where the desire to solve this problem came from.

“From the very foundation of when we decided to embark upon this effort, we recognized it has to be actually deployable, actually scalable, and not a science project,” he said. “We weren’t interested in just seeing what we could prove. We wanted to make sure it actually was something that could get into the wild and serve a purpose”

title: Google upgrades all Gemini side panels in Workspace to have the same features
snippet: Gemini in Google Workspace can now “complete complex, cross-app tasks” from whatever app you’re working in. more…
fullText:
Gemini in Google Workspace can now “complete complex, cross-app tasks” from whatever app you’re working in.

Previously, the Gemini side panels found in each Workspace app had capabilities specific to that service: “generating a personalized document with Gemini required being in Docs while building AI-powered spreadsheets required being in Sheets.”

Google is now upgrading each instance of Gemini in Workspace to have the same feature set. This applies to the side panels in Gmail, Drive, Docs, Slides, and Chat. The upgrade is made possible by Workspace Intelligence and deeper app integrations.

For example, you can have Gemini “send an email to my sales team for their review and feedback” from Google Docs instead of needing to be in Gmail. 

	

In Google Chat, you can “find open times, schedule meetings, or resolve calendar conflicts.” Google Tasks also lets you “instantly log a reminder or create a to-do list” from any service.

On the content creation front, example prompts include:

When in Gmail (via the side panel) to create a doc: “Create a strategy brief for this project with goals, milestones and next steps.“

When in Gmail (via the side panel) to create a spreadsheet: “Create a tracker for this project in a new spreadsheet”

When in Docs (via the side panel) to create a deck: “Turn this proposal into an easy to read slide deck for my director using @presentation as a style reference.”

When in Chat (via Ask Gemini in Chat) to create a document: “Create a deck outlining Project Zebra with the latest updates”

When in Drive (via Ask Gemini in Drive) to create a document: “Create a customer insights deck from project Zebra using my project files including sheets, reports, and emails”

This expanded feature set started rolling out this month. For consumers, this is available to subscribers of Google AI Pro (“with the exception of scheduling functionality”) and Google AI Ultra. It’s also coming to:

Business: Standard and Plus

Enterprise: Standard and Plus

Other Editions: Frontline Plus (only for scheduling functionality)

Education Add-ons: Google AI Pro for Education

Other Add-ons: AI Expanded Access

title: tvOS 27 removes a feature that some Apple TV users might miss after updating
snippet: When tvOS 27 is released later this month, Apple TV users will gain an overhauled Podcasts app. The new version includes Apple’s new video podcast streaming technology. However, eagle-eyed users may notice that the upcoming software update removes one feature that may be missed after updating: support for shows followed by a URL. more…
fullText:
When tvOS 27 is released later this month, Apple TV users will gain an overhauled Podcasts app. The new version includes Apple’s new video podcast streaming technology.

However, eagle-eyed users may notice that the upcoming software update removes one feature that may be missed after updating: support for shows followed by a URL.

Podcasts on Apple TV 4K gets a big update that removes a niche feature

As mentioned, Apple TV 4K is adding support for streaming HLS-based video podcasts in the Podcasts app in tvOS 27.

This follows the same feature coming to iOS 26.4’s Podcasts app on iPhone and iPad. The Mac also supports HLS video shows in macOS 27 Golden Gate.

But tvOS 27.0 lacks one feature as part of the new version. Shows added with a custom URL, like membership-only feeds for paid podcasts, no longer work on Apple TV 4K’s Podcasts app with tvOS 27.

This is likely a feature oversight or something that Apple plans to add back in the future.

Custom feeds are still supported for Apple’s Podcasts app on iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Apple Vision Pro, and Mac with the OS 27 updates.

tvOS 27 is only compatible with the second- and third-generation Apple TV 4K. The original Apple TV 4K is capped at tvOS 26 — which still supports custom URL feeds.

fullText:
Apple did the thing. The first foldable iPhone has arrived with the new iPhone Duo delivering a pretty compelling package for interested foldable customers who don’t want to give up on iOS. It also addresses a durability gap that few others have managed with IP68 protection but, like Pixel 11 Pro Fold, that’s only a temporary rating for the iPhone Duo.

In a footnote on Apple’s iPhone Duo listing, the company admits that the IP68 dust/water protection won’t last forever:

iPhone Duo is splash, water, and dust resistant and was tested under controlled laboratory conditions with a rating of IP68 under IEC standard 60529 (maximum depth of 6 meters up to 30 minutes). Splash, water, and dust resistance are not permanent conditions. Resistance might decrease as a result of normal wear…

It’s a bit less of a thought for a typical slab-style smartphone, as the dust/water resistance there shouldn’t change drastically unless there is external damage. But, with a foldable, there are moving parts to account for and, as such, the rating may wane over time.

Apple’s not alone.

	

Google was the first to manage an IP68 rating on a foldable with last year’s Pixel 10 Pro Fold, a spec that’s since carried on to the Pixel 11 Pro Fold. In Google’s own footnote, the company explains:

Designed to comply with dust and water protection rating IP68 under IEC standard 60529 when each device leaves the factory but the device is not water or dust proof. The accessories are not water or dust resistant. Water resistance and dust resistance are not permanent conditions and will diminish or be lost over time due to normal wear and tear, device repair, disassembly or damage. Phone is not drop/tumble proof and dropping your device may result in loss of water/dust resistance.

As pointed out in our comments, Google also carries the same disclaimer on standard Pixel phones, but the same isn’t true of every brand. Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro listings, for example, don’t mention anything about the water resistance waning. Honor does say the same about its Magic V6 foldable, with the IP68/69 rating “not permanently effective, and the protective performance may decrease due to daily wear and tear,” with the same disclaimer on Magic 8 Pro. Foldables are still more prone to this problem than typical slab smartphones, though.

Still, it’s good to see that Apple is getting right out of the gate with IP68 on the iPhone Duo. Samsung, for comparison, still lacks the heightened dust resistance of the three devices mentioned here, with IP48 dust/water resistance on the latest Galaxy foldables.

title: The incomplete history of Duo devices
snippet: Apple announced the company's first device with a folding screen today, the iPhone Duo, but that's where the firsts end. The Duo is not only far from the first foldable on the market thanks to the efforts of Samsung and Google, but it's also not the first product to be called the Duo. Former Apple CEO Steve Jobs popularized the saying "good artists copy, great artists steal," but will the iPhone Duo's folding screen, which features a custom nano-texture display material to help minimize the visibility of its crease, be enough to make us forget these other Duos that have come before it? Only time, or how aggressively Apple plans to market i … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Apple announced the company’s first device with a folding screen today, the iPhone Duo, but that’s where the firsts end. The Duo is not only far from the first foldable on the market thanks to the efforts of Samsung and Google, but it’s also not the first product to be called the Duo.

Former Apple CEO Steve Jobs popularized the saying “good artists copy, great artists steal,” but will the iPhone Duo’s folding screen, which features a custom nano-texture display material to help minimize the visibility of its crease, be enough to make us forget these other Duos that have come before it? Only time, or how aggressively Apple plans to market its Duo, will tell. Is there a Duo we missed? Let us know.

NEC TurboDuo

Merging the functionality of the TurboGrafx-16 console and the TurboGrafx-CD that added CD-ROM functionality, the NEC TurboDuo (later rebranded to just the Duo) launched in North America in 1993 after debuting in Japan a few years earlier as the PC Engine Duo. The console was developed as part of a joint venture between NEC and Hudson Soft but never reached the popularity of the original TurboGrafx-16; its short run ended on Christmas Day in 1995.

Google Duo

Photo by Dieter Bohn / The Verge

First released in 2016 and eventually merged into Google Meet in 2022, Google Duo was the company’s proprietary VoIP service meant to compete with products like Skype or Zoom and replace Hangouts. Its cross-platform availability included Android and iOS mobile devices as well as web browsers, and while it supported hi-def video calls, the service was also optimized for slow mobile networks.

Apple PowerBook Duo

The iPhone Duo isn’t even Apple’s first Duo. The PowerBook Duo predates everything Apple announced today by decades. It was an ultraportable laptop, and when Apple introduced it in 1992 it was the smallest and lightest PowerBook available, but still weighed over 4 pounds. Apple managed to shrink the Duo using an approach it still uses today: omitting built-in ports and expansion features. If you wanted to connect peripherals and accessories you had to rely on optional docks. If you’ve ever had to buy a USB hub to connect all your devices to your MacBook, you can thank the PowerBook Duo.

Apple MagSafe Duo

Photo by Dieter Bohn / The Verge

Twenty-three years after the PowerBook Duo was discontinued, the company announced the MagSafe Duo charger that could wirelessly charge an iPhone and an Apple Watch at the same time. However, it felt like a consolation prize for the Apple AirPower wireless charger, which was announced in 2017 but never materialized. The MagSafe Duo was discontinued just a few years later in late 2023, paving the way for the foldable iPhone to steal its identity.

Microsoft Surface Duo

Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge

That’s right, the iPhone Duo isn’t even the first folding mobile device to be called the Duo. Microsoft’s Surface Duo launched in 2020 and managed to get around the issues with early foldables like the Samsung Galaxy Fold, which debuted a year prior, by skipping flexible screen technology altogether. Microsoft’s Duo instead had a very visible hinge between its pair of 5.6-inch OLED screens. But software issues, a disappointing camera, and outdated specs when it launched all resulted in the Surface Duo’s failure, even with an improved Duo 2 that launched a year later.

Asus ROG Zephyrus Duo

Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge

Trade shows are the birthplace of weird laptops, but sometimes the prototypes that often debut just to draw visitors to booths make it into the mainstream. Such was the case with the Asus ROG Zephyrus Duo, a powerful gaming laptop with excellent specs, a wildly expensive price tag, and a pair of 16-inch OLED screens that can be vertically stacked or placed side by side.

Asus ZenBook Pro Duo

Photo: Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge

The ROG Zephyrus Duo wasn’t Asus’ first attempt at creating a dual-screen laptop, or the first time it named a laptop a Duo. The ZenBook Pro Duo predates it by several years with a slightly different design. Beneath the ZenBook Pro Duo’s primary 15.6-inch OLED screen was a secondary 14-inch display located above the laptop’s keyboard. With an ultrawide 32:9 aspect ratio and less color fidelity, the smaller screen was designed to be a place to dock productivity tools like Slack or Gmail so they were still readily accessible but less of a distraction while working (or gaming) on the primary display.

Pebble 2 Duo

After convincing Google to open-source the Pebble’s operating system last year, Eric Migicovsky, the creator of what was arguably one of the first truly successful and capable smartwatches, resurrected the wearable under a new company called Core Devices. The Pebble 2 Duo, one of the first smartwatches from Migicovsky’s new company, isn’t as capable as the Apple Watch or devices running Android’s Wear OS, but its careful balance of simplicity, functionality, and a budget-friendly price make it a tempting alternative.

iRobot Roomba Duo

Photo: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

It’s still just a prototype and may never find its way into consumers’ homes, but at IFA 2026 in Berlin last week, iRobot debuted the bizarre Roomba Duo. The prototype includes a beefy mobile dock with clean and dirty water tanks and the most powerful floor-cleaning suction the company has ever made. To ensure it can clean all areas in your home, atop the Roomba Duo is a deployable garage with a smaller Roomba Plus 757 inside that can easily fit into tight spaces and beneath furniture.

Retroid Pocket Duo

Image: Retroid

Mere hours before the iPhone Duo made its debut, Retroid revealed the full design of its latest dual-screen handheld it’s been teasing. The Retroid Pocket Duo is a modernized version of the Nintendo DS with dual 120Hz OLED screens featuring a 16:9 aspect ratio on top and a 4:3 aspect ratio between its controls. Full specs and pricing aren’t confirmed yet, but the Pocket Duo features a symmetrical dual thumbstick design, two pairs of shoulder buttons, and a headphone jack.

snippet: Motorola hasn’t had a proper flagship in the US in quite some time, but a brief appearance of “Signature 27” hints that might change in the coming months. more…
fullText:
Motorola hasn’t had a proper flagship in the US in quite some time, but a brief appearance of “Signature 27” hints that might change in the coming months.

The Motorola Signature launched in early 2026 as the first big launch in quite a while that (mostly) fits the “flagship” bill. High-end materials, solid specs, and no slouch in software updates either. It was fairly compelling, but never saw a US debut. 

For a brief little while earlier this week, Motorola’s website was showing a banner teasing the “Signature 27,” an apparent successor to the initial Signature release. There’s little here to confirm it’s coming to the US market, but it’s hard to imagine any other reason for this to show up on the US site at all. 

	

The banner has since vanished across all of Motorola’s sites, suggesting it was probably posted too early. The first Motorola Signature launched in January, and the “Signature 27” name alone suggests this one is at least a couple more months away from launch.

title: How to fast charge iPhone 18 Pro
snippet: The new iPhone 18 Pro has much better battery life than its predecessors, but it also has even faster wired charging. To fast charge the new iPhone, Apple says you need to use its dynamic 40-watt power adapter with 60-watt max output and USB-C cable. With this combination, you will charge at the maximum possible speed, which is about 33% faster than previous pro iPhones could. more…
fullText:
The new iPhone 18 Pro has much better battery life than its predecessors, but it also has even faster wired charging.

To fast charge the new iPhone, Apple says you need to use its dynamic 40-watt power adapter with 60-watt max output and USB-C cable. With this combination, you will charge at the maximum possible speed, which is about 33% faster than previous pro iPhones could. 

Maximum charging speed on iPhone 18 Pro with a 60-watt charger means you can charge from zero to 50% in about 15 minutes. That’s about 5 minutes faster than iPhone 17 Pro, for comparison.

Also, at that faster charging rate, Apple says users can get about 6 hours of video playback time with just a quick five minute top-up charge.

Specifically, Apple’s specs for the new iPhone 18 fast charging times require a 60-watt USB PD 3.1-compatible power adapter with Adjustable Voltage Supply feature. Right now, the only charger readily available that meets those requirements is the Apple 40W dynamic power adapter.

When we get the phones in our hands, we’ll be able to do some hands-on battery charge time tests with other third-party adapters to see how they fare. For instance, the MacBook charger you already own will likely be rated for 96W or 140W, but it lacks the Adjustable Voltage Supply feature. 

There are also a bunch of third-party chargers rated above 40-watts, like this Anker 45W brick. Presumably, iPhone 18 Pro will achieve the same as iPhone 17 Pro did here, fast charging from empty to 50% in about twenty minutes. This is still very fast charging when you are in a pinch.

For wireless charging, iPhone 18 Pro can go from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes when paired with the Apple MagSafe Charger and any 35-watt power brick.

iPhone 18 Pro goes up for preorder this Saturday, with first units shipping on September 18. When Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo ships next month, it will also support the same faster charging speeds as iPhone 18 Pro, if you have the right accessories as described above. 

Remember, Apple doesn’t include power bricks with their phones anymore — just a USB-C cable.

title: Apple’s revamped Health app will calculate your ‘health age’ and readiness score
snippet: The update uses Apple Intelligence to make better sense of your health data.
fullText:
Alongside the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, Apple on Wednesday introduced a redesigned Apple Health app that takes advantage of Apple Intelligence to make better sense of your health data. The changes deliver a new Insights tab that includes a summary of the most timely information, plus personalized guidance, assessments, a new “readiness” score, and a computation of your “Health Age.”

The latter is a way to understand how your various health metrics compare with your actual age and uses data like your VO2 max, sleep, and more, including biomarkers from your blood.

Image Credits:Apple

The additions also include a new Longevity tab, which uses metrics from your Apple Watch and iPhone to assess your health across sleep, movement, heart health, and other factors. Your lab results can be incorporated into this guidance, and Apple announced a team-up with Quest for a 50-biomarker panel for $119, giving users quick access to data that can only come from lab tests.

Image Credits:Apple

With Apple Intelligence, Apple’s Health app has been improved to make sense of other health data, too, which comes into play in features like the readiness score and the Insights tab. For instance, the app could suggest that a user incorporate more intervals into their morning run to improve their cardio health. The app will also go deeper in areas like fitness and heart health as well, Apple said.

The Health app also allows users to take in-depth assessments of how well their bodies are moving, which can help people who are older or recovering from an injury. A trainer can even demonstrate certain moves for you to try as you take the assessment, which Apple claims is like having a coach right there with you.

The updated Health app rolls out later this year, starting in U.S. English.

title: Apple announces A20 Pro chip with 2nm design and major performance gains
snippet: Apple today unveiled the A20 Pro, its first chip built on 2nm technology at its “Surprise and Shine” event, bringing major CPU, GPU, and AI upgrades to the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple today unveiled the A20 Pro, its first chip built on 2nm technology at its “Surprise and Shine” event, bringing major CPU, GPU, and AI upgrades to the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Here are the details.

Apple announces A20 Pro chip

Apple today unveiled the A20 Pro chip, which will power the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

The A20 Pro features a new architecture built on 2nm technology, with smaller and more densely packed transistors that Apple says enable upgrades across the entire chip.

The new A20 Pro chip packs six CPU cores, featuring two supercores that Apple says are 20% faster, alongside four efficiency cores. All are integrated with neural accelerators for low-latency AI workloads.

The A20 Pro’s GPU has a seven-core design, which Apple says enables up to a 40% performance increase. Apple also introduced a new version of its neural accelerators, with 2x faster 8-bit floating-point math, aimed at advanced AI workloads such as running third-party LLMs on-device.

The Neural Engine has also been upgraded with a second engine, bringing the total to 32 cores and delivering twice the compute performance.

Apple says these CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine improvements are supported by a 50% increase in memory bandwidth, enabled by what it calls the widest memory interface ever shipped in an iPhone.

The A20 Pro also introduces a new packaging design inspired by Apple’s M-series chips, placing the silicon die side by side with the memory. According to Apple, this removes the memory from the SoC’s thermal path and allows the silicon to connect directly to its next-generation vapor chamber, significantly improving thermal performance.

To support the iPhone Duo’s dual-display design, the A20 Pro also features a new display engine that drives both displays simultaneously and enables smooth transitions between them.

Apple says it also blends the unique pixel layout around the under-display camera area of the iPhone Duo to deliver a consistent visual experience.

title: Apple invites developers to submit browser interoperability ideas for Interop 2027
snippet: Apple’s WebKit team is inviting developers to submit their ideas for Interop 2027, the next edition of the cross-browser initiative aimed at improving web interoperability. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple’s WebKit team is inviting developers to submit their ideas for Interop 2027, the next edition of the cross-browser initiative aimed at improving web interoperability. Here are the details.

A bit of context

Over the past few years, Apple has collaborated with Google, Microsoft, Mozilla, Bocoup, and Igalia on Interop, an annual effort to make modern web technologies work more consistently across different browsers.

The project began in 2022, building on the earlier Compat initiative, with participating browser makers and organizations identifying 15 key areas where interoperability issues were creating problems for web developers. While Compat was originally conceived as a one-off effort, it proved successful, and Interop has returned every year since.

Each year, the group selects a new set of focus areas, based in part on proposals from the web development community. Browser makers then work to improve their implementations in those areas, with progress measured through a shared set of Web Platform Tests.

Earlier this year, the WebKit team shared the results of Interop 2025, which saw the percentage of selected tests passing across all browsers jump from just 29% at the beginning of the year to 97% by the end.

They also outlined the 20 focus areas selected for Interop 2026, spanning CSS features and technologies such as the Navigation API, View Transitions, WebRTC, and WebTransport, partly based on proposals submitted by the web development community during last year’s open call.

Which brings us to this year’s open call, which officially opened on September 3 and will accept proposals through September 23.

Interop 2027 entries now open

Apple says that proposals must be based on mature web standards and be testable, since nascent technologies aren’t ready to become Interop Focus Areas, and the project relies on automated Web Platform Tests to measure progress across browsers. The company also notes that technologies that lack sufficient tests or testing infrastructure should instead be proposed as Interop Investigations.

Here’s what Apple says makes a “great” Interop 2027 proposal:

The best submissions are typically:

Specific: Identify a specific interoperability issue. One feature (or narrow group of related features) per proposal. Think font-size-adjust, not “typography”.

Impactful: Provide a clear description of the interoperability problem that needs addressing. Use cases from your own experience are especially helpful.

Valuable: Explain how web developers and/or users will benefit. Why is this more valuable than other existing options? Is there evidence this is a common need (perhaps survey results)?

Stable: Link to the stable web standard that defines the technology you want improved. (Find it on the MDN web doc for that technology. Like here.)

Tested: Look up and link to WPT test coverage. If more tests are needed, how can they be created this fall?

Read the Interop Proposers Guide to learn more.

The company also notes that developers should be mindful that not everyone reading this year’s proposals will have full knowledge of last year’s proposals, and that they must “take the time needed to fully make” their case.

That includes explaining why the proposed focus area is important, how the current state of affairs affects web developers and users, how widely the technology is used, and why addressing the issue should be a priority over other potential focus areas.

Developers can submit their own proposals by filing an issue on GitHub, or support an existing proposal by adding comments that help strengthen its case. Apple says it is better to contribute to an existing issue than to submit multiple proposals covering the same or very similar ideas.

title: iPhone Duo is thicker and heavier than basically every Android foldable
snippet: The days of foldables being an Android-only experience are over. The iPhone Duo is set to arrive next month for a relatively-competitive $2,000 price point, and it seems like Apple’s decision to sit back and observe since the launch of the original Galaxy Fold more or less paid off — that is, until you consider the iPhone Duo’s size and shape. more…
fullText:
The days of foldables being an Android-only experience are over. The iPhone Duo is set to arrive next month for a relatively-competitive $2,000 price point, and it seems like Apple’s decision to sit back and observe since the launch of the original Galaxy Fold more or less paid off — that is, until you consider the iPhone Duo’s size and shape.

I won’t lie — there’s plenty of things I find intriguing about the iPhone Duo. Sure, it apes almost everything we know about modern folding phones from Samsung and Google, but with a couple of interesting twists. Keeping the under-display camera and stylus support from earlier Galaxy Z-series entries? A very smooth transition between inner and outer displays? A Made You Look clone but with Snoopy? I might prefer Android to iOS, but at the end of the day, I’m only human.

But no matter how “modern” the iPhone Duo appears at first glance compared to Google and Samsung’s respective first-gen entries, it loses out on one big metric: bulk. The iPhone Duo measures in at 11.3mm thick when closed and weighs a whopping 254 grams. Compared to Apple’s most recent foldable rivals, that’s 15 grams (or three nickels worth) heavier than the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, 39 grams heavier than the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, and a whopping 53 grams heavier than the similarly-shaped Fold 8. Each of those phones is significantly thinner too, ranging anywhere between 8.9mm to 10.1mm when closed.

iPhone Duo: 254g, 11.3mm closed

Pixel 11 Pro Fold: 239g, 10.1mm closed

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra: 215g, 8.9mm closed

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: 201g, 9.7mm closed

It is, undoubtedly, a miss from Apple’s design, especially considering the push for lightweight devices with last year’s iPhone Air. However — and here’s where I have betray the most dedicated Android fans just a tiny bit — while I absolutely think Apple’s foldable is bulkier and heavier than it should be in 2026, I can’t pretend like Google is that far ahead here. Yes, this year’s foldable finally managed to shed a few grams, but the iPhone Duo still manages to be lighter than 2025’s Pixel 10 Pro Fold, a device Google was pushing to users but a month ago. Samsung, though? It’s eating Apple’s lunch all day.

	

I also have no idea how much of that extra bulk can be chalked up to Apple Pencil support. Samsung upset a pretty sizable portion of its audience when it dropped the S Pen from the Galaxy Z Fold 7, but that sacrifice came with a significantly slimmer and lighter chassis. Comparing the iPhone Duo to 2024’s Fold 6 — the last foldable Samsung shipped with stylus support — it measures in at 12.1mm thick. That said, the Fold 6 still had Apple beat on weight, even with a device that’s now over two years old.

At the end of the day, the size and weight of the iPhone Duo really only matters if you’re completely platform-agnostic, a foldable-first fan who simply wants the most refined hardware experience around. I expect most Android fans won’t be tempted with a big-screen experience not all too dissimilar from what they’ve had access to for the better part of a decade now, and I expect iOS fans who have held out for an Apple-made foldable won’t be put off by a device that’s a bit bulkier than its rivals. But hey, if you’re an early adopter looking to lord something over your Apple-loving co-workers in a couple of months, you’ve already found your first opportunity.

title: Pixel 11 gets early September update, not Android 17 QPR1 [U: OTA images]
snippet: We’re expecting the stable release of Android 17 QPR1 in September. Before that, Google is rolling out an out-of-cycle update to the Pixel 11 series with a September 2026 security patch. more…
fullText:
We’re expecting the stable release of Android 17 QPR1 in September. Before that, Google is rolling out an out-of-cycle update to the Pixel 11 series with a September 2026 security patch.

Update 9/9: Following the on-device update that some users received last week, Google has posted updated factory and OTA images for manual install. The September 1 patch ended in A1, while today’s release is B1.

It comes as not all users received last week’s OTA, with Google appearing to pull the update at some point. Those that received the previous update are getting another one that comes in at 97~ MB.  

The four updates for the Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold are labeled “Sep 2026.” Curiously, Google has yet to announce the Android 17 QPR1 update and expected Pixel Drop.

	

Original 9/1: On Tuesday afternoon, Pixel 11 series users received an OTA update to CD1A.260905.001.A1 (from CD1A.260714.001.A9).

The Android security update level is “September 1, 2026.” (Note: Not September 5.) The install screen has the usual generic security message: “This update fixes critical bugs and improves the performance and stability of your device.”

So far, we have reports of an under 100 MB OTA hitting the Pixel 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold. Google has yet to post factory or OTA images as of Tuesday afternoon.

This is not Android 17 QPR1. Several of the visual changes coming in that release are not yet present, so this is still the initial release of Android 17.

Rather, Google is likely rolling out this update as a hot patch for Pixel 11 issues discovered since last month’s launch. The fact Google did not wait for Android 17 QPR1 should be telling.
